2) Keep the shin parallel to the floor while pressing back.

instructions.instructions: From standing, bend your right knee to 90-degrees behind you (shin parallel to the floor), so that you're balancing on your left leg. Remain completely upright and use a wall or other object for balance if necessary as you lift your thigh out to the side and as high as possible. Keep the hips square to the front. Avoid shifting your weight sideways as you lift; feel the outside of your right hip work hard to lift your leg. Pause at your end range and then, keeping your knee at the same height, slowly slide your leg back behind you. Slide it as far as you can without losing height, pause, and return the top of the standing abduction position. Repeat the backward slide for reps before lowering your leg and switching sides.

focusPoints.description: 1) To count, each rep must begin and end in the hsPL.
2) The body must be horizontal at full extension.

instructions.instructions: Begin kneeling on all fours with your hands rotated outward approximately 45-degrees. With locked elbows and protracted and depressed shoulders, begin to lean forward. As you lean, allow your feet to lift off the ground and your legs to come apart. Continue angling forward until your hips reach shoulder height. Open your hips, keep your knees bent to 90-degrees, and straddle as wide as you can. Now extend your legs while continuing to straddle wide with both hips open. Pause briefly and return to the half straddle planche. Repeat the double leg extension for reps. Avoid bobbing up and down during the extensions; keep a stable planche position throughout. Be sure your shoulder blades remain strongly depressed and protracted to maximize your leverage. To keep your hips open you must maintain a significant forward lean.

focusPoints.description: 1) Minimize the sideways lean.
2) The effort for lifting the leg must come from the hip.

instructions.instructions: Begin seated on the floor with your legs hip-width apart. Bend your knees and hips to approximately 90-degrees and place your feet flat on the floor. Keep your torso as upright as possible and drop both knees down to your right side. The outside of your right leg and inside of your left should now be in contact with the floor. Adjust your torso so that you're facing your right leg. Check that both of your knees are bent to 90-degrees, and lift your entire left leg off the floor with control. Be sure your left foot, knee, and thigh lift off at the exact same time. Raise your leg as high as possible, pause momentarily, and place your leg back down with control. Repeat for reps, ensuring you keep your torso upright and the rest of your body stationary to better isolate the outside of your left hip.

focusPoints.description: 1) Begin and end in the half straddle planche position.
2) Note that both legs are in constant motion.

instructions.instructions: Begin kneeling on all fours with your hands rotated outward approximately 45-degrees. With locked elbows and protracted and depressed shoulders, begin to lean forward. As you lean, allow your feet to lift off the ground and your legs to come apart. Continue angling forward until your hips reach shoulder height. Open your hips, keep your knees bent to 90-degrees, and straddle as wide as you can. Now extend your right leg while continuing to straddle wide with both hips open. Pause briefly and as you retract your right leg, begin to extend your left. Continue to alternate leg extensions for reps. Avoid bobbing up and down during the extensions; keep a stable planche position throughout. Be sure your shoulder blades remain strongly depressed and protracted to maximize your leverage. To keep your hips open you must maintain a significant forward lean. Be sure to always have both legs working during the set but begin and end each in the half straddle planche.

focusPoints.description: 1) The ankle and knee raise up simultaneously and remain parallel to the ground for the duration of the set.

instructions.instructions: Begin seated on the floor with your legs hip-width apart. Bend your knees and hips to approximately 90-degrees and place your feet flat on the floor. Keep your torso as upright as possible and drop both knees down to your right side. The outside of your right leg and inside of your left should now be in contact with the floor. Adjust your torso so that you're facing your right leg. Check that both of your knees are bent to 90-degrees, and lift your entire left leg off the floor with control. Be sure your left foot, knee, and thigh lift off at the exact same time. Raise your leg as high as possible and hold for time before placing your leg back down with control. Be sure you keep your torso upright and the rest of your body stationary to better isolate the outside of your left hip. Switch and hold on your opposite leg to finish the set.

focusPoints.description: 1) Maximally protract and depress the scapula.
2) The hips must remain completely open to count the set.

instructions.instructions: Begin kneeling on all fours with your hands rotated outward approximately 45-degrees. With locked elbows and protracted and depressed shoulders, begin to lean forward. As you lean, allow your feet to lift off the ground and your legs to come apart. Continue angling forward until your hips reach shoulder height. Open your hips, keep your knees bent to 90-degrees, and straddle as wide as you can. Now extend your legs while continuing to straddle wide with both hips open. Once your legs are completely extended, maintain the position and hold for time. Be sure your shoulder blades remain strongly depressed and protracted to maximize your leverage. To keep your hips open and legs extended you must maintain a significant forward lean.

focusPoints.description: 1) After lifting, the lower leg should directly extend backward as far as possible along a straight line.

instructions.instructions: Begin seated on the floor with your legs hip-width apart. Bend your knees and hips to approximately 90-degrees and place your feet flat on the floor. Keep your torso as upright as possible and drop both knees down to your right side. The outside of your right leg and inside of your left should now be in contact with the floor. Adjust your torso so that you're facing your right leg. Check that both of your knees are bent to 90-degrees, and lift your entire left leg off the floor with control. Be sure your left foot, knee, and thigh lift off at the exact same time. Raise your leg as high as possible and pause at your end range. Then, keeping your knee at the same height, slowly slide it back behind you. Slide it as far as you can without losing height, pause, and return the top of the seated abduction position. Repeat the backward slide for reps before lowering your leg and switching sides.

Begin kneeling on the floor and place your palms down flat, fingers facing your knees. Fully straighten your elbows and lean back. Keep your palms pressed firmly into the floor as you lean. When you feel a good stretch through your wrists and forearms, pause briefly, and repeat for reps or hold for time. Increase the intensity of the stretch by moving your hands further from your knees.

Begin kneeling on the floor and place the back of your hands down flat, fingers facing your knees. Fully straighten your elbows and lean back. Keep your entire hand pressed firmly into the floor as you lean. When you feel a good stretch through your wrists and forearms, pause briefly, and repeat for reps or hold for time. Increase the intensity of the stretch by moving your hands further from your knees. To scale, if straightening your elbows is not possible right now, keep your shoulders stacked over your wrists and either perform reps straightening your elbows as much as possible or hold your straightest elbow position for time.

Begin kneeling on the floor and place your palms down flat, fingers facing away from your knees. Fully straighten your elbows and lean forward. Keep your palms pressed firmly into the floor as you lean. When you feel a good stretch through your wrists and forearms, pause briefly, and repeat for reps or hold for time. Increase the intensity of the stretch by moving your hands closer to your knees.

Begin kneeling on the floor and place your palms down flat, fingers facing away from your knees. Rotate both hands inward so your pinkies face inward. Now fully straighten your elbows. If you can't, you have rotated too far inward. With straight elbows and hands pressed firmly into the floor, lean backward. When you feel a good stretch through your wrists and forearms, pause briefly, and repeat for reps or hold for time. If you are particularly tight and your best position with straight elbows is fingers facing each other, lean side-to-side rather than backward. Over time, aim to rotate further inward, ultimately rotating your hands 180-degrees.

focusPoints.description: 1) Bend the wrists one at a time so that the back of the hand and wrist are flush with the wall.

instructions.instructions: Stand an arm's-length away from a wall, fully extend your arms, and press your fists against it at shoulder-height (thumbs facing up). Slowly lower the back of your right hand toward the wall and aim to get it completely flat on the wall. Pause briefly and slowly use your wrist to press back to your fist. Repeat on the left, and continue to switch sides for the set, never bending your elbows. The slower you perform this wrist walk, the more productive it will be. If you cannot get your hand flat on the wall with a straight elbow, just go as far as you can for now; do not bend your elbow just to get your hand flat. Keep your arms parallel to the floor at all times.

focusPoints.description: 1) The slower the tempo the more productive this exercise is.

instructions.instructions: Stand an arm's-length away from a wall, fully extend your arms, and press your fists against it at approximately chest-height (thumbs facing up). Now, keep your fists in place on the wall and step back into a long hollow. Check that your body is straight from shoulders to ankles, and is at approximately a 45-degree angle to the wall. Keep this long hollow shape, with posterior pelvic tilt, and slowly lower the back of your right hand toward the wall. Aim to get it completely flat, pause briefly, and slowly use your wrist to press back to your fist. Repeat on the left, and continue to switch sides for the set, never bending your elbows. The slower you perform this wrist walk, the more productive it will be. If you cannot get your hand flat on the wall with a straight elbow, reduce the angle of your long hollow; do not bend your elbow just to get your hand flat. Keep your arms parallel to the floor at all times.

focusPoints.description: 1) If necessary, at first you may decrease the intensity of this exercise by piking the hips.

instructions.instructions: Begin kneeling on all fours, supported on your fists (placed directly below your shoulders) with your thumbs facing forward. Slowly lower the back of your right hand toward the floor and aim to get it completely flat. Pause briefly and slowly use your wrist to press back to your fist. Repeat on the left, and continue to switch sides for the set, never bending your elbows. The slower you perform this wrist walk, the more productive it will be. If you cannot get your hand flat on the floor with a straight elbow, move your hands closer to your knees; do not bend your elbow just to get your hand flat. Keep your arms perpendicular to the floor at all times.

focusPoints.description: 1) Do not allow the elbows to bend, concentrate solely on full extension through each wrist.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a straight arm plank, supported on your fists (placed directly below your shoulders) with your thumbs facing forward. Slowly lower the back of your right hand toward the floor and aim to get it completely flat. Pause briefly and slowly use your wrist to press back to your fist. Repeat on the left, and continue to switch sides for the set, never bending your elbows. The slower you perform this wrist walk, the more productive it will be. If you cannot get your hand flat on the floor with a straight elbow, use an easier wrist walk progression to build more strength; do not bend your elbow just to get your hand flat. Keep your arms perpendicular to the floor at all times.

focusPoints.description: 1) This is my favorite all wrist variations; it allows for a very slow intense movement which you will feel deep in the joint.

instructions.instructions: Stand an arm's-length away from a wall, fully extend your arms, and press your fists against it at shoulder-height (thumbs facing up). Slowly lower the back of your hands toward the wall while simultaneously bending your elbows. Bend until the backs of your hands are completely flat on the wall. Allow your elbows to flare out; this will keep your hands in line. Pause briefly on the backs of your hands and slowly press back to your fists. The slower you perform these standing wrist push-ups, the more productive they will be. Use the push-up portion of the movement as a secondary aide to ascend and descend; wrist strength should drive the motion. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Note that it is necessary to flare the elbows to the side in order to keep the hands parallel.

instructions.instructions: Stand an arm's-length away from a wall, fully extend your arms, and press your fists against it at approximately chest-height (thumbs facing up). Now, keep your fists in place on the wall and step back into a long hollow. Check that your body is straight from shoulders to ankles, and is at approximately a 45-degree angle to the wall. Keep this long hollow shape, with posterior pelvic tilt, and slowly lower the backs of your hands toward the wall while simultaneously bending your elbows. Bend until the backs of your hands are completely flat on the wall. Allow your elbows to flare out; this will keep your hands in line. Pause briefly on the backs of your hands and slowly press back to your fists. The slower you perform these long hollow wrist push-ups, the more productive they will be. Use the push-up portion of the movement as a secondary aide to ascend and descend; wrist strength should drive the motion. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) The thumbs are elevated during the ascent and descent to keep the stress fully on the wrists.

instructions.instructions: Begin kneeling on all fours, supported on your fists (placed directly below your shoulders) with your thumbs facing forward. Slowly lower the back of your hands toward the floor while simultaneously bending your elbows. Bend until the backs of your hands are completely flat on the floor. Allow your elbows to flare out; this will keep your hands in line. Pause briefly on the backs of your hands and slowly press back to your fists. The slower you perform these kneeling wrist push-ups, the more productive they will be. Use the push-up portion of the movement as a secondary aide to ascend and descend; wrist strength should drive the motion. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Do not allow the wrist to simply flop down; rather lower the back of the wrist with strength and control.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a straight arm plank, supported on your fists (placed directly below your shoulders) with your thumbs facing forward. Slowly lower the back of your hands toward the floor while simultaneously bending your elbows. Bend until the backs of your hands are completely flat on the floor. Allow your elbows to flare out; this will keep your hands in line. Pause briefly on the backs of your hands and slowly press back to your fists. The slower you perform these kneeling wrist push-ups, the more productive they will be. Use the push-up portion of the movement as a secondary aide to ascend and descend; wrist strength should drive the motion. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) The goal is to bend the first knuckles a full 90 degrees.

instructions.instructions: Stand an arm's-length away from a wall, fully extend your arms, and place your hands flat at shoulder-height (fingers facing up). Slowly lift your right palm, bending at the base of your fingers. Continue to bend at your first knuckles until they are bent to a 90-degree angle. Pause briefly and then lower your palm back to flat. Repeat on the left, and continue to switch sides for the set, never bending your elbows. If you cannot bend to 90-degrees, just go as far as you can for now. Keep your arms parallel to the floor at all times and never let your fingers come off of the wall.

focusPoints.description: 1) Often times due to too much desk work, the fingers and hence the wrists get too tight without our even noticing.

instructions.instructions: Stand an arm's-length away from a wall, fully extend your arms, and place your hands flat on it at approximately chest-height (fingers facing up). Now, keep your hands in place on the wall and step back into a long hollow. Check that your body is straight from shoulders to ankles, and is at approximately a 45-degree angle to the wall. Keep this long hollow shape, with posterior pelvic tilt, and slowly lift your right palm, bending at the base of your fingers. Continue to bend at your first knuckles until they are bent to a 90-degree angle. Pause briefly at your end range and then lower your palm back to flat. Repeat on the left, and continue to switch sides for the set, never bending your elbows. Keep your arms parallel to the floor at all times and never let your fingers come off of the wall.

focusPoints.description: 1) Take advantage of the extra support provided by going one hand at a time to really focus on stretching the fingers.

instructions.instructions: Begin kneeling on all fours, hands flat, placed directly below your shoulders (fingers forward). Slowly lift your right palm, bending at the base of your fingers. Continue to bend at your first knuckles until they are bent to a 90-degree angle. Pause briefly at your end range and then lower your palm back to flat. Repeat on the left, and continue to switch sides for the set, never bending your elbows. Keep your arms vertical at all times and never let any part of your fingers come up.

focusPoints.description: 1) Keep the fingers flat on the floor as the knuckles are bending.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a straight arm plank with your hands flat, directly below your shoulders (fingers forward). Slowly lift your right palm, bending at the base of your fingers. Continue to bend at your first knuckles until they are bent to a 90-degree angle. Pause briefly at your end range and then lower your palm back to flat. Repeat on the left, and continue to switch sides for the set, never bending your elbows. Keep your arms vertical at all times and never let any part of your fingers come up.

focusPoints.description: 1) Let the palms go flat at the bottom of each repetition.

instructions.instructions: Stand an arm's-length away from a wall, fully extend your arms, and place your hands flat at shoulder-height (fingers facing up). Bend your elbows and perform a push-up against the wall. When you return to the top of the wall push-up, lift your palms, bending at the base of your fingers. Continue to bend at your first knuckles until they are bent to a 90-degree angle. Pause briefly and then lower your palms back to flat. Keep your hands in place on the wall and keep full finger-to-wall contact throughout. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Strive to keep the shoulders open in full flexion during this variation.

instructions.instructions: Stand an arm's-length away from a wall, fully extend your arms, and place your hands flat on it at approximately chest-height (fingers facing up). Now, keep your hands in place on the wall and step back into a long hollow. Check that your body is straight from shoulders to ankles, and is at approximately a 45-degree angle to the wall. Keep this long hollow shape, with posterior pelvic tilt, Bend your elbows and perform a push-up against the wall. When you return to the top of this long hollow push-up, lift your palms, bending at the base of your fingers. Continue to bend at your first knuckles until they are bent to a 90-degree angle. Pause briefly and then lower your palms back to flat. Keep your hands in place on the wall and keep full finger-to wall contact throughout. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Even under this greater load, remember to continue bending the knuckles a full 90 degrees.

instructions.instructions: Begin kneeling on all fours, hands flat, placed directly below your shoulders (fingers forward). Bend your elbows and perform a kneeling push-up. When you return to the top of this kneeling push-up, lift your palms, bending at the base of your fingers. Continue to bend at your first knuckles until they are bent to a 90-degree angle. Pause briefly and then lower your palms back to flat. Keep your hands in place on the floor and keep full finger-to-floor contact throughout. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Continue to move with as slow a speed as you can manage; remember that the fingers must remain flat.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a straight arm plank with your hands flat, directly below your shoulders (fingers forward). Bend your elbows and perform a push-up. When you return to the top of the push-up, lift your palms, bending at the base of your fingers. Continue to bend at your first knuckles until they are bent to a 90-degree angle. Pause briefly and then lower your palms back to flat. Keep your hands in place on the floor and keep full finger-to-floor contact throughout. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Although the ROM is relatively limited, these are a potent exercise as this area of the wrist receives little conditioning.

instructions.instructions: Stand an arm's-length away from a wall, fully extend your arms, and press your fists against it at shoulder-height (thumbs facing up). Keep your elbows straight and roll your right fist upward until the top is in contact with the wall. You should now be on the side of your index finger. Pause in the stretch and return to the start position. Now bend your right elbow and roll your right fist down until the bottom of it touches the wall. You should now be on the side of your little finger and bottom of your fist. Pause again and return to the start. Be sure to keep your left wrist and arm still as your right rocks up and down. Switch sides and continue to alternate for the set, only bending your elbow when rocking a fist downward. Keep tight fists as you rock up and down for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) The wrist bending to the front while turned sideways is called "ulnar deviation".

instructions.instructions: Stand an arm's-length away from a wall, fully extend your arms, and press your fists against it at chest-height (thumbs facing up). Now, keep your hands in place on the wall and step back into a long hollow shape. Keep a straight body (maintain posterior pelvic tilt) and roll your right fist upward until the top is in contact with the wall. You should now be on the side of your index finger. Pause in the stretch and return to the start position. Now bend your right elbow and roll your right fist down until the bottom of it touches the wall. You should now be on the side of your little finger and bottom of your fist. Pause again and return to the start. Be sure to keep your left wrist and arm still as your right rocks up and down. Switch sides and continue to alternate for the set, only bending your elbow when rocking a fist downward. Keep tight fists as you rock up and down for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) The wrist bending to the rear while turned sideways is called "radial deviation".

instructions.instructions: Begin kneeling on all fours, supported on your fists (placed directly below your shoulders) with your thumbs facing forward. Keep your elbows straight and roll your right fist forward until only the top is in contact with the floor. You should now be on the side of your index finger. Pause in the stretch and return to the start position. Now bend your right elbow and roll your right fist backward until only the bottom of it touches the floor. You should now be on the side of your little finger and bottom of your fist. Pause again and return to the start. Be sure to keep your left wrist and arm still as your right rocks forward and backward. Switch sides and continue to alternate for the set, only bending your elbow when rocking a fist downward. Keep tight fists as you rock forward and backward for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Performing these from a plank can be rather intense; leaning to one side will help you to scale these if needed.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a straight arm plank, supported on your fists (placed directly below your shoulders) with your thumbs facing forward. Keep your elbows straight and roll your right fist forward until only the top is in contact with the floor. You should now be on the side of your index finger. Pause in the stretch and return to the start position. Now bend your right elbow and roll your right fist backward until only the bottom of it touches the floor. You should now be on the side of your little finger and bottom of your fist. Pause again and return to the start. Be sure to keep your left wrist and arm still as your right rocks forward and backward. Switch sides and continue to alternate for the set, only bending your elbow when rocking a fist downward. Keep tight fists as you rock forward and backward for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Build the ROM on these gradually; the intensity of working both wrists at the same time can sneak up on you.

instructions.instructions: Stand an arm's length away from a wall, fully extend your arms, and press your fists against it at shoulder-height (thumbs facing up). Keep your elbows straight and roll your fists upward until the tops are in contact with the wall. You should now be on the sides of your index fingers. Pause in the stretch and return to the start position. Now bend your elbows and roll your fists down until the bottom of them touches the wall. You should now be on the sides of your little fingers and bottom of your fists. Pause again and return to the start. Keep tight fists as you rock up and down for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Be sure that the primary focus during the radial deviation is on the wrist bending and not on the elbow bending.

instructions.instructions: Stand an arm's-length away from a wall, fully extend your arms, and press your fists against it at chest-height (thumbs facing up). Now, keep your hands in place on the wall and step back into a long hollow shape. Keep a straight body (maintain posterior pelvic tilt) and roll your fists upward until the tops are in contact with the wall. You should now be on the side of your index fingers. Pause in the stretch and return to the start position. Now bend your elbows and roll your fists down until the bottom of them touches the wall. You should now be on the sides of your little fingers and bottom of your fists. Pause again and return to the start. Keep tight fists as you rock up and down for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Focus on making the transition between ulnar and radial deviation smooth.

instructions.instructions: Begin kneeling on all fours, supported on your fists (placed directly below your shoulders) with your thumbs facing forward. Keep your elbows straight and roll your fists forward until only the tops are in contact with the floor. You should now be on the side of your index fingers. Pause in the stretch and return to the start position. Now bend your elbows and roll your fists backward until only the bottom of them touch the floor. You should now be on the side of your little fingers and bottom of your fists. Pause again and return to the start. Keep tight fists as you rock forward and backward for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Keep the elbows completely locked during the ulnar deviation of the wrist (sideways forward bend).

instructions.instructions: Begin in a straight arm plank, supported on your fists (placed directly below your shoulders) with your thumbs facing forward. Keep your elbows straight and roll your fists forward until only the tops are in contact with the floor. You should now be on the sides of your index fingers. Pause in the stretch and return to the start position. Now bend your elbows and roll your fists backward until only the bottom of them touch the floor. You should now be on the side of your little fingers and bottom of your fists. Pause again and return to the start. Keep tight fists as you rock forward and backward for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) our fingers may be bending in all directions on your first attempt at these; they will straighten as strength improves.

instructions.instructions: Stand an arm's-length away from a wall, fully extend your arms, and place your hands flat (fingers together) against it at shoulder-height. Press through your right fingertips and lift your hand off the wall, keeping your fingers straight and in contact with it. Lift until you have a straight line from your right shoulder to your right fingertips (parallel to the floor). Lower back down and switch sides, alternating hands for reps. Keep tension in your working hand as it moves up and down. Also ensure you move with control and that your elbows remain straight. It is normal to have contact with only your middle three fingers at the top of reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Smoothly transition from one hand to the other; extending and flexing the fingers strongly.

instructions.instructions: Stand an arm's-length away from a wall, fully extend your arms, and place your hands flat (fingers together) just below chest height. Now, keep your hands in place on the wall and step back into a long hollow. Check that your body is straight from shoulders to ankles, and is at approximately a 45-degree angle to the wall. Keep this long hollow shape, with posterior pelvic tilt, and press through your right fingertips while lifting your hand off the wall, keeping your fingers straight and in contact with it. Lift until you have a straight line from your right shoulder to your right fingertips (parallel to the floor). Lower back down and switch sides, alternating hands for reps. Keep tension in your working hand as it moves up and down. Also ensure you move with control and that your elbows remain straight. It is normal to have contact with only your middle three fingers at the top of reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Leaning to one side will reduce the intensity of this exercise, but do not lean more than needed.

instructions.instructions: Begin kneeling on all fours, hands flat and fingers together, placed directly below your shoulders. Press through your right fingertips and lift your hand off the floor keeping your fingers straight and in contact with the ground. Lift until you have a straight line from your right shoulder to your right fingertips (perpendicular to the floor). Lower back down and switch sides, alternating hands for reps. Keep tension in your working hand as it moves up and down. Also ensure you move with control and that your elbows remain straight. It is normal to have contact with only your middle three fingers at the top of reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Completely extend the knuckles at the top of each repetition; there should be no bend in the fingers.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a straight-arm plank with your hands flat and fingers together, directly below your shoulders. Press through your right fingertips and lift your hand off the floor keeping your fingers straight and in contact with the ground. Lift until you have a straight line from your right shoulder to your right fingertips (perpendicular to the floor). Lower back down and switch sides, alternating hands for reps. Also ensure you move with control and that your elbows remain straight. Keep your elbows straight at all times and move with control.  It is normal to have contact with only your middle three fingers at the top of reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) The fingers should be neither arched nor piked; but rather perfectly straight.

instructions.instructions: Stand arms-length away from a wall, fully extend your arms, and place your hands flat against it at shoulder-height. Be sure your fingers are together and not spread apart. Bend your elbows and perform a push-up against the wall. When you return to the top of the wall push-up, press through your fingertips and lift your hands off the wall, keeping your fingers straight and in contact with it. Lift until you have a straight line from your shoulders to your fingertips (parallel to the floor). Descend with control and repeat for reps. Keep tension in your hands as they move up and down. Also ensure you move with control and that your elbows remain straight. It is normal to have contact with only your middle three fingers at the top of reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) The intensity of these can be either increased or decreased according to the depth of the long hollow hold.

Also ensure you move with control and that your elbows remain straight. It is normal to have contact with only your middle three fingers at the top of reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Due to the support of the knees it is natural for these to lean back slightly during the ascent.

instructions.instructions: Begin kneeling on all fours, hands flat and fingers together, placed directly below your shoulders. Bend your elbows and perform a kneeling push-up. When you return to the top of this kneeling push-up, press through your fingertips and lift your hands off the floor keeping your fingers straight and in contact with the ground. Lift until you have a straight line from your shoulders to your fingertips (perpendicular to the floor). Descend with control and repeat for reps. Keep tension in your hands as they move up and down. Also ensure you move with control and that your elbows remain straight. It is normal to have contact with only your middle three fingers at the top of reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Attempt to pause for a second or two at the top of each repetition.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a straight arm plank with your hands flat and fingers together, directly below your shoulders. Bend your elbows and perform a push-up. When you return to the top of the push-up, press through your fingertips and lift your hands off the floor, keeping your fingers straight and in contact with the ground. Lift until you have a straight line from your shoulders to your fingertips (perpendicular to the floor). Descend with control and repeat for reps. Keep tension in your hands as they move up and down. Also ensure you move with control and that your elbows remain straight. It is normal to have contact with only your middle three fingers at the top of reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Think of creating a triangle of support; with the head at the top and the hands as the two lower corners.

instructions.instructions: To set up, kneel on the floor (sitting on your heels) and place your hands flat just in front your knees. Lean forward and place the crown of your head about a foot in front of your hands, so that your elbows form a 90-degree angle. Now place one knee at a time onto the back of your arms. Find your balance in the tripod and hold still for time.

Mobility.name: Static Seated Shoulder Flexion with Weighted Bar

focusPoints.description: 1) Using a weighted bar (5lb minimum) tilt forward and "pull" the hands behind the head.

instructions.instructions: Begin sitting cross legged on the floor. Grab a weighted bar with a shoulder-width grip and raise it overhead. Shrug your shoulders to your ears, straighten your elbows, and sit up tall. Pull your arms behind your ears, tighten your core, and lean forward, hinging at your hips. As you lean forward, you must maintain a maximal shoulder shrug and keep a straight line from your hips to your hands. Hold the forward lean for time. If the bar drops down and your shoulder angle closes, reset and try again with a more suitable weight and/or forward lean.

focusPoints.description: 1) If your hands are properly placed, the fingers should be just barely visible from the corner of the eyes.

instructions.instructions: To set up, kneel on the floor (sitting on your heels) and place your hands flat just in front your knees. Lean forward and place the crown of your head about a foot in front of your hands, so that your elbows form a 90-degree angle. Press evenly through your hands to press your legs up over your hips, straightening your body in an inverted headstand position. Squeeze your abdominals and glutes, fully straighten your knees, and point your toes. Hold still for time.

Mobility.name: Static Standing Shoulder Extension with Weighted B

focusPoints.description: 1) Strive to elevate the bar until it is level with the shoulders.
2) Remain upright with a flat back as the bar is raised.

instructions.instructions: Begin standing with a weighted bar held behind your glutes, palms forward. At first, use as wide a grip as necessary but aim to move narrower over time. Keep your body fully upright, retract your shoulder blades (pinch them together), and lift the bar up behind you with straight elbows. Keep retracting, lift the bar as high as possible, and hold for time at your end range.

focusPoints.description: 1) Cup the back of the head with the hands.
2) The entire forearm should be used to balance.

instructions.instructions: Begin kneeling on the floor with your hands interlocked behind your head. Fold forward and place your head and forearms on the floor just in front of your knees. Keep even pressure through your head and forearms. Press your legs up over your hips, straightening your body in an inverted forearm stand position. Squeeze your abdominals and glutes, fully straighten your knees, and point your toes. Hold still for time.

Mobility.name: Seated Shoulder Flexion Reps with Weighted Bar

focusPoints.description: 1) Do not rush through these reps.
2) Maximize the R.O.M. during each of the leans forward.

instructions.instructions: Begin sitting cross legged on the floor. Grab a weighted bar with a shoulder-width grip and raise it overhead. Shrug your shoulders to your ears, straighten your elbows, and sit up tall. Pull your arms behind your ears, tighten your core, and lean forward, hinging at your hips. As you lean forward, you must maintain a maximal shoulder shrug and keep a straight line from your hips to your hands. Pause momentarily, return to the start position, and repeat for reps. If the bar drops down and your shoulder angle closes, reset and try again with a more suitable weight and/or forward lean.

Strength.name: Supine Floor Handstand Flexion with Weighted Bar

focusPoints.description: 1) Keep the ribs pulled down and the upper back flat.
2) Do not allow the lower back to arch or come off the floor.

instructions.instructions: To set up, lie on your back, body extended, and place a weighted bar across your thighs. Engage your abs and press your ribs down until your lower back makes full contact with the floor. Keep this posterior pelvic tilt (PPT) and full back-to-floor contact throughout. Hold the bar at shoulder-width and begin to raise it overhead. Stop just before you lose PPT and hold. Your goal is to be able to hold the bar just off of the ground for time. During the hold, elevate your scapula completely by shrugging your shoulders up to your ears the entire time.

Mobility.name: Standing Shoulder Extension with Weighted Bar

focusPoints.description: 1) A shoulder width grip is your ultimate goal.
2) Feel the chest open and the shoulders pull back.

instructions.instructions: Begin standing with a weighted bar held behind your glutes, palms forward. At first, use as wide a grip as necessary but aim to go narrower over time. Keep your body fully upright, retract your shoulder blades (pinch them together), and lift the bar up behind you with straight elbows. Keep retracting, lift the bar as high as possible, pause briefly at your end range, and lower back down with control. Repeat this action for reps.

Strength.name: Prone Floor Handstand Flexion with Weighted Bar

Hold the bar with a shoulder-width grip, shrug your shoulders to your ears as much as possible, and lift the bar high. Keep your elbows 100% straight, chin down, and chest down, as you hold for time.

Mobility.name: Standing Overgrip Dislocate with Weighted Bar

focusPoints.description: 1) Begin wide and over time make your grip narrower.
2) Once weight increases, widen the grip and begin again.

Widen your overgrip (palms back) to at least double shoulder-width and raise the bar overhead with straight elbows. As the bar begins to pass overhead shrug up strongly (elevate your shoulders). Once the bar is overhead, roll your shoulders inward and lower the bar behind you, all the way to your glutes. Reverse the motion back to the front and repeat for reps. Never let your elbows bend, always shrug as the bar goes overhead, and keep a firm grip. Over time, work to slowly narrow your grip to nearly shoulder-width.

Strength.name: Prone Floor Handstand Flexion Pulses with Weighted Bar

2) Do not lift either the chin or the chest off the floor.

Once the bar reaches its highest point, lower it down to just off the floor, and continue to pulse up and down with control. Keep your elbows 100% straight, chin down, and chest down as you repeat for reps.

Hold for time, ultimately building to sets of 30 seconds.

Mobility.name: Prone Overgrip Dislocate with Weighted Bar

focusPoints.description: 1) This should be a smooth, rolling movement.

Continue lifting until the bar travels 180-degrees around to your glutes. Reverse the motion, returning the bar to the floor with control, and repeat for reps. focusPoints.description: 1) The fingers must touch the shoulder for the rep to count.
2) Feel the supporting arm extend upward.

Check that your body is straight, your pelvis is posteriorly tilted, and your shoulders are elevated (shrug to your ears). Shift some weight to your right arm and take your left off the ground. Tap your left shoulder with your left hand, place it back on the floor, and switch sides. Build to 30 taps per set and work on developing a fluid rhythm.

Mobility.name: Prone Undergrip Dislocate with Weighted Bar

focusPoints.description: 1) Do not jerk the weight, pull it smoothly from the floor.
2) Slowly lower the weight behind, do not allow it to drop!

instructions.instructions: Lie on your stomach, body straight, and a weighted bar placed across your glutes. Look up slightly so that your chin, and not your forehead, is in contact with the floor. Hold the bar with at least a double shoulder-width grip, palms down. Lift the bar up and around 180-degrees and place it down overhead on the floor. Reverse the motion, returning the bar to your glutes with control, and repeat for reps. Never let your elbows bend, always shrug as the bar goes overhead, and keep a firm grip. Over time, work to slowly narrow your grip to nearly shoulder-width.

focusPoints.description: 1) Feel the chest and upper thighs in contact with the wall.
2) Do not allow the lower back to arch.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a straight arm plank with your feet at the base of a wall. Keep a straight body and walk your feet up the wall until your hands are within 6 to 12 inches of it. Check that your body is straight, your pelvis is posteriorly tilted, and your shoulders are elevated (shrug to your ears). Maintain open shoulders (180-degree flexion). For this wall handstand progression, focus on maintaining contact to the wall with your chest and hips. Hold for time, ultimately building to sets of 60 seconds.

focusPoints.description: 1) Mastering PPT is essential for good body alignment.
2) Glutes and upper back remain in contact with the wall.

instructions.instructions: Stand about 1 foot from a wall, facing away. Sit back into the wall, bend your knees slightly. Support yourself in this high wall sit position for the duration. Engage your abs, pulling your ribs down flat until you feel you lower back press into the wall. Hold this position and check that you have wall contact from waist to head. Now disengage your core, allowing your ribs to flare out, and let your lower back come off of the wall. Alternate between these two positions for reps: arched lower back (anterior pelvic tilt/APT) and flat back (posterior pelvic tilt/PPT). Be sure your waist, upper back, and head remain in contact with the wall at all times, allowing only your lower back to move forward and backward. Practice controlling and feeling the difference between APT and PPT to improve your pelvic control for handstands and other bodyweight exercises.

focusPoints.description: 1) Do not allow the lower back or the shoulders to sag or loose tension at any time during the set.

Check that your body is straight, your pelvis is posteriorly tilted, and your shoulders are elevated (shrug to your ears). Shift some weight to your right arm and take your left off the ground. Tap your left shoulder with your left hand, place it back on the floor, and switch sides. Build to 60 taps per set and work on developing a fluid rhythm.

focusPoints.description: 1) Beginning with the arch first helps you to better feel the opposite or correct position when trying to achieve PPT.

instructions.instructions: Lie flat on your stomach, legs together and arms out to your sides in the letter T. Look up slightly so that your chin, and not your forehead, is in contact with the floor. Engage your core, squeeze your glutes, and straighten your knees until your quads engage. Hold these contractions and try to feel your tail tuck under and a space form between your lower stomach and the floor. This is a posterior pelvic tilt (PPT). Now relax, sticking your butt up in the air while arching your lower back. This arched position is an anterior pelvic tilt (APT). Alternate between these two positions, APT and PPT, for reps to improve pelvic control for handstands and other bodyweight exercises. Work to keep the rest of your body still as you switch back and forth.

focusPoints.description: 1) The hands will now be within 1-3" of the wall.
2) Note that his hips are not in contact with the wall.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a straight arm plank with your feet at the base of a wall. Keep a straight body and walk your feet up the wall until your hands are within 1 to 3 inches of it. Maintain a straight body line, with posterior pelvic tilt (PPT), 180-degree shoulder flexion, and complete scapular elevation (shoulder shrug) throughout the static hold. For this wall handstand progression, focus on maintaining a straight body line; when this close to the wall, your hips should not be touching it if your pelvis is properly tilted. Hold for time, ultimately building to sets of 60 seconds.

focusPoints.description: 1) If you are successful with the PPT, all of the arch will be taken out of your lower back.

Engage your abs, pulling your ribs down flat until your feel your lower back press into the floor. Hold this position and check that you have floor contact from waist to head. Now disengage your core, allowing your ribs to flare out, and let your lower back come off of the floor. Alternate between these two positions for reps: arched lower back (anterior pelvic tilt/APT) and flat back (posterior pelvic tilt/PPT). Be sure your waist, upper back, and head remain in contact with the floor at all times, allowing only your lower back to move up and down. Practice controlling and feeling the difference between APT and PPT to your improve your pelvic control for handstands and other bodyweight exercises.

focusPoints.description: 1) Brace somewhere between the mid and upper forearms.

Stop when your hands reach the base of the support and your forearms are lightly touching its entire outer face. Slowly take your feet off the wall, achieve a straight handstand line, and press your forearms into the support, using it as a balance aide. Maintain a posterior pelvic tilt and hold for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) Do not allow the legs to lift off the ground during the PPT.
2) Keep the upper and lower back, glutes and legs flat.

Engage your abs, pulling your ribs down flat until your feel you lower back press into the floor. Hold this position and check that you have floor contact from waist to head. Now disengage your core, allowing your ribs to flare out, and let your lower back come off of the floor. Alternate between these two positions for reps: arched lower back (anterior pelvic tilt/APT) and flat back (posterior pelvic tilt/PPT). Be sure everything but your low back remains still and in contact with the floor at all times. Only your lower back should move up and down. Practice controlling and feeling the difference between APT and PPT to your improve pelvic control for handstands and other bodyweight exercises.

focusPoints.description: 1) Use an overhead support that your toes can barely reach.
2) Reaching the bar should require complete extension.

Kick up into a handstand and fully extend through your body: point your toes, straighten your legs, achieve a posterior pelvic tilt (PPT), and open and shrug your shoulders strongly. If the overhead support is properly positioned, it should be unreachable without fully lengthening your body. Hold this assisted handstand for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) It is normal to feel somewhat unstable at first.
2) Focus on a smooth transition between the PPT and arch.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a forearm plank, with your shoulders stacked above your elbows. Spread your shoulder blades apart (protract) and achieve a posterior pelvic tilt (PPT) by squeezing your abs and glutes. Engage your core, squeeze your glutes, and straighten your knees until your quads engage. Hold these contractions and try to feel your tail tuck under and your lower back flatten. This is a posterior pelvic tilt (PPT). Now relax, sticking your butt up in the air while arching your lower back. This arched position is an anterior pelvic tilt (APT). Alternate between these two positions, APT and PPT, for reps to improve pelvic control for handstands and other bodyweight exercises. Work to keep the rest of your body still as you switch back and forth.

focusPoints.description: 1) Note that only the leg on the wall breaks body alignment.
2) The pull off the wall should be very slow and deliberate.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a wall handstand, hands placed about one foot away from the wall, with your hips slightly piked. Pull one foot off the wall and over your hips. Hold this handstand briefly. Maintain a straight body line, with posterior pelvic tilt (PPT), 180-degree shoulder flexion, and complete scapular elevation (shoulder shrug) throughout the static hold. Now bring one foot back to the wall at a time, back to the start position. Repeat this partial wall handstand for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) PPT becomes more difficult when the core is loaded.
2) Focus on moving the hips only; not the entire back.

Spread your shoulder blades apart (protract) and achieve a posterior pelvic tilt (PPT) by squeezing your abs and glutes. Work to keep the rest of your body still as you switch back and forth.

focusPoints.description: 1) Feel a flat back, ribs down and posterior pelvic tilt (PPT) before beginning.
2) Control the handstand with the hands and wrists.

Hold this handstand briefly. Maintain a straight body line, with posterior pelvic tilt (PPT), 180-degree shoulder flexion, and complete scapular elevation (shoulder shrug) throughout the static hold. focusPoints.description: 1) To achieve proper PPT the hips should have no change in elevation, but rather a change in rotation.

Now place your feet onto a box (1-3 feet high) and press your hips up until your body straightens. Engage your abs and glutes, pulling your ribs down flat. Hold this position and check that you have a straight line from feet to shoulders. Now disengage your core, allowing your ribs to flare out, and let your lower back to arch. Alternate between these two positions for reps: arched lower back (anterior pelvic tilt/APT) and flat back (posterior pelvic tilt/PPT). Practice controlling and feeling the difference between APT and PPT to your improve pelvic control for handstands and other bodyweight exercises.

Engage your abs, pulling your ribs down flat until your feel you lower back press into the floor. Maintain this posterior pelvic tilt (PPT) and raise your legs up off the floor until you have a 90-degree bend at your waist. Lower your legs back down until they are just above the floor and repeat for reps. Never allow your low back to lose floor contact or your ribs to flare during the set.

focusPoints.description: 1) Pull the legs out sideward, do not allow them to drop forward.
2) Move slowly and deliberately, no jerking or rushing.

instructions.instructions: Kick up into a properly aligned free handstand. Hold the handstand and straddle your legs apart as wide as you can while not allowing them to drift forward or backward. Once your best straddle is achieved, pull your legs back together. Move slowly and smoothly as you repeat for reps.

Lower back down to the floor with control and repeat for reps. Keep your elbows and knees straight at all times. Control the handstand by pressing your wrists forward and backward. Build up to 10-second static holds.

focusPoints.description: 1) It is not necessary for the beginning arch to be extreme.
2) Keep the body tight and extended for the duration.

Keep your elbows and knees straight at all times. Shrug your shoulders to your ears (elevate) and maintain a posterior pelvic tilt throughout. Keep your body tight and extended as you hold for time.

2) Keeping the shoulders extended will help to avoid arching.

If your head is positioned properly, you should just barely be able to see your fingertips out of the corner of your eyes. Build up to 30-second static holds.

instructions.instructions: Stand within one inch from a wall, facing it, with your arms overhead and shoulders fully elevated. Tighten your core and, with your hands flat on the wall, walk backward until your extended body is at a 45-degree angle. Achieve and maintain posterior pelvic tilt (PPT) to prevent your body from piking. Hold for time, keeping a tight, extended position throughout.

focusPoints.description: 1) Only the shoulders should move during this element.
2) Do not allow the head to move; stay steady.

Hold the handstand steady and depress your shoulders. You should drop down slightly and create a small space between your shoulders and ears. Elevate back to the start position and repeat for reps as you hold a still free handstand, moving only your shoulders through elevation and depression.

2) Do not allow any change in alignment during the walk out.

Keep your body straight and walk out to a 45-degree angle. Maintain a posterior pelvic tilt (PPT) and fully open shoulders (180-degree flexion). Hold the long hollow for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) Note that the hips get over the shoulders very quickly.

Maintain a straight body line, with posterior pelvic tilt (PPT), 180-degree shoulder flexion, and complete scapular elevation (shoulder shrug) throughout the static hold. Control the handstand by pressing your wrists forward and backward. Build up to 30-second static holds.

focusPoints.description: 1) Do not allow the legs to bend during the descent.
2) Lowering all the way down and back up is one rep.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a wrist-to-wall handstand (belly-to-wall) with proper alignment and walk your hands out. Creep your feet down the wall as you walk out. Keep your body in the same alignment, with posterior pelvic tilt (PPT) and fully open shoulders (180-degree flexion), and continue to walk out away from the wall until you reach a long hollow on the floor. Pause briefly and then walk back up the wall with the same body position until you reach a wrist-to-wall handstand again. Repeat this long hollow wall walk for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Working on too soft a surface will cause wrist fatigue.
2) Calm shallow breathing is necessary during a long HS.

Spread your shoulder blades apart (protract) and achieve a posterior pelvic tilt (PPT) by squeezing your abs and glutes. Walk your hands forward until your shoulders fully open and your body is suspended just above the floor in a long hollow position. Remember to fully elevate your shoulders as you walk out. focusPoints.description: 1) Keep the descending foot next to the other leg.

Ensure your moving foot remains close to your straight leg and stacked over your glutes as your knee bends and straightens. Repeat for reps.

Spread your shoulder blades apart (protract) and achieve a posterior pelvic tilt (PPT) by squeezing your abs and glutes. Walk your hands forward until your shoulders fully open and your body is suspended just above the floor in a long hollow position. Remember to fully elevate your shoulders as you walk out. Be sure to maintain PPT throughout. Hold this long hollow for time.

Lift your hands first, then head, and, finally, your chest and legs at the same time. Arch high, pause briefly, and lower back to the floor. Keep body extension and tension, press through your hands and feet, and lift up into a long hollow. Be sure to achieve a posterior pelvic tilt (PPT) as early as possible. Pause, lower back to the floor, and repeat for reps.

Pause briefly before extending your legs back up. Ensure your feet remain stacked over your glutes as your knees bend and straighten. Repeat for reps.

Walk your hands out away from the wall until your body is at a 45-degree angle. Now achieve and maintain proper body line, with posterior pelvic tilt (PPT), complete scapular elevation (shoulder shrug), and open shoulders. Feel your traps burn as they fight to maintain shoulder flexion. Also note that PPT in this position feels as though you are piked. Hold for time.

2) Note how the body automatically went to alignment.

2) Finish with the scapula both protracted and elevated.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a straight arm plank position (shoulders over your wrists) with your feet elevated to shoulder height. Be sure your elbows and knees are straight, your body is parallel to the floor, and your shoulder blades are spread apart (protracted). Keep your feet and hands in place and press your chest back toward your feet. As you press backward and invert your upper body, shrug your shoulders strongly toward your ears. Shoulder protraction and elevation are key to this progression so emphasize those positions as you press. Pause at your end range, when you feel a good stretch and your shoulders are open (a straight line from hips to hands). Return to the start position and repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) At a minimum, attempt to sink into the pike until the hips are below the hands at the bottom of the movement.

instructions.instructions: Stand with your back to stall bars or a similar apparatus and place both feet together on the bottom rung. Grab on behind you to the bar closest to waist height, palms forward, and weight your arms. With locked elbows and knees, grip tight and slowly fold forward into a pike stretch while simultaneously allowing your hips to drop down. As you sink down into the inverted pike stretch, stretch your torso long across your legs. Once you’ve reached your end range, pull back up to the start position. Keep your arms and legs straight and repeat for reps. Take the stretch deeper by reducing the space between your hands and feet. Close the space between your upper and lower body and aim to eventually get your legs parallel with the floor.

focusPoints.description: 1) Focus on pressing downward into the ground.
2) The main pressure is on the hands; feet are secondary.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a straight arm plank position (shoulders over your wrists). Keep your elbows straight and begin walking your feet toward your hands. As you walk, stay on your tiptoes, shrug your shoulders strongly toward your ears, and keep your arms perpendicular to the floor. Do not lean forward as you walk. Keep as much weight in your hands as possible; imagine lifting your feet off the floor. Pause in your best position, walk your feet back to the plank, and repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) The knees and elbows must remain completely straight.
2) Do not fidget; remain still for the duration.

instructions.instructions: Stand with your back to stall bars or a similar apparatus and place both feet together on the bottom rung. Grab on behind you to the bar closest to waist height, palms forward, and weight your arms. With locked elbows and knees, grip tight and slowly fold forward into a pike stretch while simultaneously allowing your hips to drop down. As you sink down into the inverted pike stretch, stretch your torso long across your legs. Hold your best stretch for time. Take the stretch deeper by reducing the space between your hands and feet. Close the space between your upper and lower body and aim to eventually get your legs parallel with the floor.

focusPoints.description: 1) Initially begin with mats stacked as high as necessary.
2) Completing these with mats only knee high is your goal.

instructions.instructions: Stand between two hip to knee high supports. Place your feet on a slider and assume a front support position. Spread your shoulder blades apart (protract) and with straight elbows and knees, slide forward to rear support. Open your chest to stretch momentarily. Now reverse the motion, pressing back to rear support. As you press back, strongly protract and elevate your shoulder blades; push into the supports and shrug. Repeat this slide press for reps. As your strength improves, gradually lower the height of the supports. Maintaining proper form with knee height supports is a good long term goal for this exercise.

focusPoints.description: 1) Begin from your deepest inverted pike position.
2) Remain as deep as possible during the knee bends.

instructions.instructions: Stand with your back to stall bars or a similar apparatus and place both feet together on the bottom rung. Grab on behind you to the bar closest to waist height, palms forward, and weight your arms. With locked elbows and knees, grip tight and slowly fold forward into a pike stretch while simultaneously allowing your hips to drop down. As you sink down into the inverted pike stretch, stretch your torso long across your legs. Hold your best position and then gently bend your knees. Straighten them again, staying as low as possible in the inverted pike, and repeat this subtle knee bend for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) The goal is to press upward until you achieve knee height.
2) Protracting and elevating will maximize your strength.

instructions.instructions: Stand at the edge of a tall box or other stable surface that allows you to press into support on its edge. Press up through your hands. Keep your legs straight and toes pointed while keeping them in contact with the side of the box. Use a slider if necessary to press through your arms to slide your feet up. As you press, keep your elbows straight and strongly elevate and protract your shoulder blades. If your shoulders are properly positioned, your back should curl and not arch during this movement. Slide up until your knees reach hand height. Hold the top position briefly and control the descent. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) The goal is to increase the depth of your straddle until only 1 to 2 empty rails separate your hands and feet.

instructions.instructions: Stand with your back to stall bars or a similar apparatus, straddle your feet wide, and place both on the bottom rung. Grab a bar between your legs at about mid-thigh height, palms forward, and weight your arms. With locked elbows and knees, grip tight and slowly fold forward into a straddle stretch while simultaneously allowing your hips to drop down. As you sink down into the inverted straddle stretch, keep your back as straight as possible. Once you’ve reached your end range, pull back up to the start position. Keep your arms and legs straight and repeat for reps. Take the stretch deeper by reducing the space between your hands and feet. Close the space between your upper and lower body and aim to eventually get your legs parallel with the floor.

focusPoints.description: 1) The goal is to press upward until you reach mid-shin height.
2) Curl the back during the press; do not arch.

instructions.instructions: Stand at the edge of a tall box or other stable surface that allows you to press into support on its edge. Press up through your hands. Keep your legs straight and toes pointed while keeping them in contact with the side of the box. Use a slider if necessary to press through your arms to slide your feet up. As you press, keep your elbows straight and strongly elevate and protract your shoulder blades. If your shoulders are properly positioned, your back should curl and not arch during this movement. Slide up until the middle of your shins reach hand height. Hold the top position briefly and control the descent. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Give the body time to settle to its deepest point of stretch before beginning to count the 30 seconds duration.

instructions.instructions: Stand with your back to stall bars or a similar apparatus, straddle your feet wide, and place both on the bottom rung. Grab a bar between your legs at about mid-thigh height, palms forward, and weight your arms. With locked elbows and knees, grip tight and slowly fold forward into a straddle stretch while simultaneously allowing your hips to drop down. As you sink down into the inverted straddle stretch, keep your back as straight as possible. Hold your best position for time. Take the stretch deeper by reducing the space between your hands and feet. Close the space between your upper and lower body and aim to eventually get your legs parallel with the floor.

focusPoints.description: 1) The goal is to press upward until you achieve ankle height.
2) Elevate & protract until you feel the upper back cramping!

instructions.instructions: Stand at the edge of a tall box or other stable surface that allows you to press into support on its edge. Press up through your hands. Keep your legs straight and toes pointed while keeping them in contact with the side of the box. Use a slider if necessary to press through your arms to slide your feet up. As you press, keep your elbows straight and strongly elevate and protract your shoulder blades. If your shoulders are properly positioned, your back should curl and not arch during this movement. Slide up until your ankles reach hand height. Hold the top position briefly and control the descent. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Take a moment to ensure that each repetition after the extension settles to its deepest point before the next rep.

instructions.instructions: Stand with your back to stall bars or a similar apparatus, straddle your feet wide, and place both on the bottom rung. Grab a bar between your legs at about mid-thigh height, palms forward, and weight your arms. With locked elbows and knees, grip tight and slowly fold forward into a straddle stretch while simultaneously allowing your hips to drop down. As you sink down into the inverted straddle stretch, keep your back as straight as possible. Hold your best position and then gently bend your knees. Straighten them again, staying as low as possible in the inverted straddle, and repeat this subtle knee bend for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Press upward off the ground and then pull the feet fwd.
2) Do not simply attempt to shuffle forward; press upward.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a standing pike fold with your hands flat on the floor about a foot in front of your feet. Place your feet together, lock your knees, and lift up onto your tiptoes. Press straight down into the floor, strongly shrugging your shoulders until your feet lift up. Once your feet have left the floor, smoothly pull them forward between your hands. Slide your hands forward about a foot, returning to your start position, and repeat this press walk for reps. Keep your shoulders open and shoulder blades both protracted and elevated throughout each set.

focusPoints.description: 1) Begin upright with the legs in a 90 degree angle.
2) Do not allow the legs to roll inward during the descent.

instructions.instructions: Sit in a straddle on the floor with your hips at approximately a 90-degree angle. Point your knees to the ceiling, lock them, engage your quads, and point your toes. Interlock your fingers behind your head and sit up completely straight with an anterior pelvic tilt (APT). If you cannot sit upright in this position, elevate your hips as high as necessary to achieve a straight back and APT in this start position. Now hinge forward at your hips and descend with a flat back until your chest makes contact with the floor. Do not allow your legs to lose tension or roll inward as you fold. Pause at the bottom momentarily, smoothly raise back up to the start position, and repeat for reps. Maintain APT throughout.

focusPoints.description: 1) Do not planche forward; keep the shoulders open.
2) Strive to get the hips on top of the shoulders.

instructions.instructions: Stand on parallettes, fold forward, and grab ahold of them just in front of your feet. Strongly shrug your shoulders to your ears, step up to your tiptoes, and continue to press down until your feet lift straight up off of the parallettes. Keep your shoulders open and avoid leaning forward to lift up. Continue pressing until your hips stack over your shoulders. Once your hips are stacked, hold your feet off the bars for time. Lower down with control to end each set and never allow yourself to planche forward.

focusPoints.description: 1) Knees remain locked, with the feet turned slightly out.
2) If you cannot grab your feet, your legs are too wide.

instructions.instructions: Sit in a straddle on the floor with your hips at approximately a 90-degree angle. Point your knees to the ceiling, lock them, engage your quads, and point your toes. Lift your arm out to your sides and sit up completely straight with an anterior pelvic tilt (APT). If you cannot sit upright in this position, elevate your hips as high as necessary to achieve a straight back and APT in this start position. Now hinge forward at your hips and descend with a flat back until your chest makes contact with the floor. Do not allow your legs to lose tension or roll inward as you fold. Hold this pancake stretch for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) Press upward into the half press before descending down into a proper straddle L with feet above the knees.

instructions.instructions: Stand on parallettes, fold forward, and grab ahold of them just in front of your feet. Strongly shrug your shoulders to your ears, step up to your tiptoes, and continue to press down until your feet lift straight up off of the parallettes. Keep your shoulders open and avoid leaning forward to lift up. Continue pressing until your hips stack over your shoulders. Once your hips are stacked, pause momentarily. To end the rep, straddle your legs wide and lower down to straddle L. Your legs must remain locked and feet must be be above your knees in the straddle L. Hold the straddle L for a moment, reset back to standing, and repeat for reps. Move steadily and never allow yourself to planche forward during this exercise.

focusPoints.description: 1) Do not allow the knees to bend or the legs to turn inward.
2) Note that the athlete keeps both glutes on the ground.

instructions.instructions: Sit in a straddle on the floor with your hips at approximately a 90-degree angle. Point your knees to the ceiling, lock them, engage your quads, and point your toes. Now sit up completely straight with an anterior pelvic tilt (APT). If you cannot sit upright in this position, elevate your hips as high as necessary to achieve APT in this start position. Hinge forward at your hips and descend with a flat back until your chest makes contact with the floor, or your lowest position. Do not allow your legs to lose tension or roll inward as you fold. Keep a flat back, reach your hands forward in front of you, and begin slowly walking your hands to the side. Walk all the way to one leg, following your hands with your body and staying flat. Switch sides and repeat this side-to-side pancake walk for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Press upward into the half press before starting to lower.
2) Do not fall out of the half press; lower with control.

instructions.instructions: Stand on parallettes, fold forward, and grab ahold of them just in front of your feet. Strongly shrug your shoulders to your ears, step up to your tiptoes, and continue to press down until your feet lift straight up off of the parallettes. Keep your shoulders open and avoid leaning forward to lift up. Continue pressing until your hips stack over your shoulders. Once your hips are stacked, pause momentarily. To end the rep, bring your feet together and lower down to an L-sit. Your legs must remain locked and your legs must remain parallel to the floor in the L-sit. Hold the L-sit for a moment, reset back to standing, and repeat for reps. Move steadily and never allow yourself to planche forward during this exercise.

focusPoints.description: 1) The hands always lift upward first, not the shoulders.
2) On each bounce, descend until almost touching the floor.

instructions.instructions: Sit in a straddle on the floor with your hips at approximately a 90-degree angle. Point your knees to the ceiling, lock them, engage your quads, and point your toes. Now sit up completely straight with an anterior pelvic tilt (APT). If you cannot sit upright in this position, elevate your hips as high as necessary to achieve APT in this start position. Hinge forward at your hips and descend with a flat back until your chest makes contact with the floor, or your lowest position. Do not allow your legs to lose tension or roll inward as you fold. Keep a flat back, reach your hands forward in front of you, and begin to bounce by pushing through your hands to the side. Bounce all the way over to one leg, following your hands with your body and staying flat. Switch sides and repeat this side-to-side pancake bounce for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) From the straddle L, now press back up to a stand.
2) Do not attempt to swing or jerk up; smoothly press up.

instructions.instructions: Stand on parallettes, fold forward, and grab ahold of them just in front of your feet. Strongly shrug your shoulders to your ears, step up to your tiptoes, and continue to press down until your feet lift straight up off of the parallettes. Keep your shoulders open and avoid leaning forward to lift up. Continue pressing until your hips stack over your shoulders. Once your hips are stacked, pause momentarily. Straddle your legs wide and lower down to straddle L. Your legs must remain locked and feet must be be above your knees in the straddle L. Hold the straddle L for a moment, press your feet back to the parallettes, and repeat for reps. Move steadily and never allow yourself to planche forward during this exercise.

focusPoints.description: 1) Note how the entire back flattens into the pancake.
2) Keep the arms and shoulders extended.

instructions.instructions: Sit in a straddle on the floor with your hips at approximately a 90-degree angle. Point your knees to the ceiling, lock them, engage your quads, and point your toes. Now sit up completely straight with an anterior pelvic tilt (APT). If you cannot sit upright in this position, elevate your hips as high as necessary to achieve APT in this start position. Hinge forward at your hips and descend with a flat back until your chest makes contact with the floor, or your lowest position. Do not allow your legs to lose tension or roll inward as you fold. Keep a flat back, reach your hands forward in front of you, and begin to sweep your hands to the side. Sweep all the way over one leg, following your hands with your body and staying flat. Sweep to the opposite leg and repeat this side-to-side pancake circle for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Now press upward from an L-sit, rather than a straddle L.
2) Press up slightly above the bar, before lowering the feet.

instructions.instructions: Stand on parallettes, fold forward, and grab ahold of them just in front of your feet. Strongly shrug your shoulders to your ears, step up to your tip-toes, and continue to press down until your feet lift straight up off of the parallettes. Keep your shoulders open and avoid leaning forward to lift up. Continue pressing until your hips stack over your shoulders. Once your hips are stacked, pause momentarily. Bring your feet together and lower down to an L-sit. Your legs must remain locked and your legs must remain parallel to the floor in the L-sit. Hold the L-sit for a moment, press your feet back to the parallettes, and repeat for reps. Move steadily and never allow yourself to planche forward during this exercise.

focusPoints.description: 1) Swing the arms forward and then pull them sideways.
2) The chest initially leans forward and then sits upright.

instructions.instructions: Sit in a straddle on the floor with your hips at approximately a 90-degree angle. Point your knees to the ceiling, lock them, engage your quads, and point your toes. Now sit up completely straight with an anterior pelvic tilt (APT). Generate momentum for the swing to straddle stand by reaching forward with your arms, leaning slightly forward with your chest, and quickly pulling your arms out to your sides. As you swing them to your sides, stand up onto your feet, keeping them at the same width on the floor. Reverse the motions to descend carefully to the floor, keep your knees locked throughout, and repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Place the hands approximately 12 inches from the wall.
2) Pausing in the tuck aids to develop better compression.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a wall handstand with your hands placed approximately one foot out. Keep proper body alignment and begin to tuck your knees toward your chest. As you begin the tuck, pull your knees apart to hip-width while keeping your feet together. As your knees get close to your chest, bring them back together and hold this wall-supported tuck handstand position momentarily. Reverse the sliding tuck back to the wall handstand and repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) The hips going backward and the chest going forward creates a counterbalance that balances the body at the bottom.

instructions.instructions: Sit in a straddle on the floor with your hips at approximately a 90-degree angle. Point your knees to the ceiling, lock them, engage your quads, and point your toes. Now sit up completely straight with an anterior pelvic tilt (APT). Reach forward with your arms, leaning slightly with your chest, and slowly pulling your arms out to your sides as you stand up. As you stand up onto your feet, keep them in the same place on the floor. Reverse the motions to descend carefully to the floor, keep your knees locked throughout, and repeat for reps.
