focusPoints.description: 1) A 30s free HS is the pre-requisite for beginning pHS/SE1.
2) Pull smoothly off the wall, do not jump off the wall.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a wall handstand with your hands placed 2-3 feet out. Keep your upper body stacked and smoothly pull your feet off the wall. Perform this partial pike press to a free handstand with proper body alignment, lower your feet back to the wall with control, and repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Remain protracted and elevated during the descent.
2) Keep the hips above the shoulders as long as possible.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a stable handstand on parallettes with proper body alignment. Slowly tuck your knees toward your chest. Once tucked, allow your spine to curl from lower back to upper until your feet reach the floor between the parallettes. During this eccentric tuck press handstand, keep your upper body in proper alignment (shoulders above your wrists) and elevate and protract strongly. Kick back up to handstand and repeat this negative press variation for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Hold the HS for at least 1-2 seconds before descending.
2) First pull the legs apart then lower thru the inv pancake.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a stable handstand on parallettes with proper body alignment. Straddle your legs wide and bend to 90-degrees at your hips. Once you reach this halfway point, allow your spine to curl from lower back to upper until your feet reach the floor. During this eccentric straddle press handstand, keep your upper body in proper alignment (shoulders above your wrists), your legs totally straight, and your shoulders elevated and protracted. Kick back up to handstand and repeat this negative press variation for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Press down strongly to fully engage the trapezius.
2) Keep the hips over the shoulders until past horizontal.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a stable handstand on parallettes with proper body alignment. Lower your legs straight down until you have a 90-degrees bend at your hips. Once you reach this halfway point, allow your spine to curl from lower back to upper until your feet reach the floor. During this eccentric pike press handstand, keep your upper body in proper alignment (shoulders above your wrists), your legs totally straight, and your shoulders elevated and protracted. Kick back up to handstand and repeat this negative press variation for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Concentrate on pulling the hips up on top of the shoulders.

instructions.instructions: From standing, with your feet together, fold forward with straight knees to place your hands flat just in front of your toes. Strongly shrug your shoulders to your ears, lift up to your tiptoes, and continue to press down until your feet come straight up off the floor. Keep your upper body stacked (shoulders over your wrists) and uncurl one vertebrae at a time. As your feet lift higher, pull your hips over your shoulders and tuck your knees to your chest. Next extend your legs straight up. Achieve a stable handstand, reverse the tuck press back to the floor, and repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Do not lean forward to start the press, this is not a PL.
2) Pull the legs out and around the sides during the press.

instructions.instructions: From a standing straddle, place your hands flat on the floor in front of you. Strongly shrug your shoulders to your ears, lift up to your tip-toes, and continue to press down until your feet come straight up off the floor. Keep your upper body stacked (shoulders over your wrists) and uncurl one vertebrae at a time. As your feet lift higher, pull your hips over your shoulders while maintaining the straddle. Continue to press your legs all the way to a straddled free handstand. Pull your feet together, and briefly hold a properly aligned handstand. Straddle your legs again and reverse the straddle press back to the floor. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) If you have been slacking on your pike mobility, you are going to find this exercise very difficult to master.

instructions.instructions: From standing, with your feet together, fold forward with straight knees to place your hands flat just in front of your toes. Strongly shrug your shoulders to your ears, lift up to your tip-toes, and continue to press down until your feet come straight up off the floor. Keep your upper body stacked (shoulders over your wrists) and uncurl one vertebrae at a time. As your feet lift higher, pull your hips over your shoulders while maintaining straight knees. Continue to press your straight legs all the way to a free handstand and briefly hold the position before reversing the pike press back to the floor. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Note the emphasis on the half press during the descent.
2) Do not allow the bottom of the movement to accelerate.

instructions.instructions: Stand on parallettes, fold forward, and grab ahold of them just in front of your feet. Strongly shrug your shoulders to your ears, step up to your tiptoes, and continue to press down until your feet lift straight up off of the parallettes. Once your feet are up, straddle wide, keep your upper body stacked (shoulders over your wrists), and uncurl one vertebrae at a time. As your feet lift higher, pull your hips over your shoulders while maintaining the straddle. Continue to press your legs all the way to a straddled free handstand, pull your feet together, and briefly hold a properly aligned handstand. Now straddle your legs wide, lower to a 90-degree hip angle, bring your feet together, and lower to an L-sit to finish. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Note the pause in the half press and L sit.
2) Focus on compression as you press back up to a stand.

instructions.instructions: Stand on parallettes, fold forward, and grab ahold of them just in front of your feet. Strongly shrug your shoulders to your ears, step up to your tip-toes, and continue to press down until your feet lift straight up off of the parallettes. Once your feet are up, straddle wide, keep your upper body stacked (shoulders over your wrists), and uncurl one vertebrae at a time. As your feet lift higher, pull your hips over your shoulders while maintaining the straddle. Continue to press your legs all the way to a straddled free handstand, pull your feet together, and briefly hold a properly aligned handstand. Now straddle your legs wide, lower to a 90-degree hip angle and pause momentarily. Bring your feet together, and lower an L-sit. Pause in the L-sit and then press your feet back up to the parallettes to finish. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Think of pulling your head under your hips in order to facilitate the press back up to the half press position.

instructions.instructions: Stand on parallettes, fold forward, and grab ahold of them just in front of your feet. Strongly shrug your shoulders to your ears, step up to your tip-toes, and continue to press down until your feet lift straight up off of the parallettes. Once your feet are up, straddle wide, keep your upper body stacked (shoulders over your wrists), and uncurl one vertebrae at a time. As your feet lift higher, pull your hips over your shoulders while maintaining the straddle. Continue to press your legs all the way to a straddled free handstand, pull your feet together, and briefly hold a properly aligned handstand. Now straddle your legs wide, lower to a 90-degree hip angle and pause momentarily. Bring your feet together, and lower an L-sit. Pause in the L-sit and then press your feet back up a half-press, pause, and lower to the parallettes to finish. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Note that there are 5 momentary pauses during each rep; HS, half press, L-sit, half press and HS.

instructions.instructions: Stand on parallettes, fold forward, and grab ahold of them just in front of your feet. Strongly shrug your shoulders to your ears, step up to your tip-toes, and continue to press down until your feet lift straight up off of the parallettes. Once your feet are up, straddle wide, keep your upper body stacked (shoulders over your wrists), and uncurl one vertebrae at a time. As your feet lift higher, pull your hips over your shoulders while maintaining the straddle. Continue to press your legs all the way to a straddled free handstand, pull your feet together, and briefly hold a properly aligned handstand. Now straddle your legs wide, lower to a 90-degree hip angle and pause momentarily. Bring your feet together and lower to an L-sit. Pause in the L-sit and then press your feet back up to perform a straddle press. Each rep ends once you have pressed back to a stable free handstand. You must have 5 distinct pauses during each rep: handstand, half press, L-sit, half press, and handstand.

focusPoints.description: 1) Feel the spine curling to the handstand; do not arch.
2) It is no longer necessary to insert pauses during the reps.

instructions.instructions: Begin in an L-sit on parallettes and begin to press to handstand. When your feet clear the parallettes, straddle your  legs wide and finish the press. At the top, bring your feet together and be sure you have a stable free handstand. Straddle your legs apart and reverse the press back to L-sit. do not allow your shoulders to planche forward; keep them stacked over your wrists at all times as you press. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) If your pike is weak, you will be tempted to planche forward.
2) Planching is unacceptable; maintain protraction & elevation.

instructions.instructions: Begin standing on the parallettes and begin to press to handstand. As soon as your feet lift off the bars, bring them together and perform a pike press. Once you are in a stable free handstand, perform a negative pike press all the way to L-sit. Pause, lower your legs, and stand up to reset. do not allow your shoulders to planche forward; keep them stacked over your wrists at all times as you press. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Pike Press HS is an essential stepping stone that must be mastered before beginning to seriously focus on OAHS.

instructions.instructions: Begin in an L-sit on parallettes and press to handstand. Keep your legs together and do not allow your shoulders to planche forward. Keep them stacked over your wrists at all times as you press from L-sit, perform a pike press, and achieve a free handstand. Reverse the press with control back to L-sit and repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Do not bend the elbows.
2) Get used to using only the wrists and shoulders to rebalance.

instructions.instructions: Set a single parallette, low bar, or dumbbells 1-2 inches from the base of a wall. Face the wall, grab the bar or dumbbells with your normal handstand width, and kick up into a back-to-wall handstand. Let your feet touch the wall and support your handstand but otherwise keep your body in proper alignment as you hold this single-bar wall handstand for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) The under-grip provides an excellent stretch for the wrists and forearms.
2) Keep the shoulders in full flexion.

instructions.instructions: Set a single parallette, low bar, or dumbbells 1-2 inches from the base of a wall. Walk up into a belly-to-wall handstand and once your hands reach the bar or dumbbells, reverse your grip to an under-grip. Your palms should now be facing away from the wall. Let your feet touch the wall and support your handstand but otherwise keep your body in proper alignment as you hold this single bar wall handstand for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) Begin with both shoulders elevated until the shoulders touch the ears.
2) Shift the shoulder over the supporting hand prior to lifting the hand off the bar.

instructions.instructions: Set a single parallette, low bar, or dumbbells 1-2 inches from the base of a wall. Face the wall, grab the bar or dumbbells with your normal handstand width, and kick up into a back-to-wall handstand. Keep your shoulders fully elevated and shift your weight over your right hand. Once your weight is all the way over to the right, lift your left hand off and bring it up to your side. Keep your body in proper alignment, hold this one arm wall handstand for time, and then switch sides.

focusPoints.description: 1) Do not lift your chin to see your hands clearly.
2) Keep the head neutral and use your peripheral vision to see the thumbs.

instructions.instructions: Set a single parallette, low bar, or dumbbells 1-2 inches from the base of a wall. Walk up into a belly-to-wall handstand and once your hands reach the bar or dumbbells, reverse your grip to an under-grip. Your palms should now be facing away from the wall. Keep your shoulders fully elevated and shift your weight over your right hand. Once your weight is all the way over to the right, lift your left hand off and bring it up to your side. Keep your body in proper alignment, hold this one arm wall handstand for time, and then switch sides.

focusPoints.description: 1) Keep the shoulder touching the ear at all times during the pirouette.
2) Do not allow the back to arch during the turn; stay tight.

instructions.instructions: Set a single parallette, low bar, or dumbbells 1-2 inches from the base of a wall. Face the wall, grab the bar or dumbbells with your normal handstand width, and kick up into a back-to-wall handstand. Let your feet touch the wall and support your handstand. Be sure you have full scapular elevation and pivot your body 90-degrees to touch your right fingertips on the floor behind your left, straight out from the wall. Your left hand should remain in position on the bar during this half pirouette. Allow your feet to come off the wall during rotation, stay tight throughout (no arching), and maintain fully elevated shoulders. Pause only briefly in this position and then press through your right hand to pivot back to the start. Switch sides and repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Complete a full 90 degree turn.
2) Use the fingertips to compensate for the height difference between the bar or block.

instructions.instructions: Set a single parallette, low bar, or dumbbells 1-2 inches from the base of a wall. Walk up into a belly-to-wall handstand and once your hands reach the bar or dumbbells, reverse your grip to an under grip. Your palms should now be facing away from the wall. Be sure you have full scapular elevation and pivot your body 90-degrees to touch your right fingertips on the floor behind your left, straight out from the wall. Your left hand should remain in position on the bar during this half pirouette. Allow your feet to come off the wall during rotation, stay tight throughout (no arching), and maintain fully elevated shoulders. Pause only briefly in this position and then press through your right hand to pivot back to the start. Switch sides and repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) An under-grip pirouette to the right immediately followed over-grip pirouette back to center constitutes one repetition.
2) Begin the next repetition with an under-grip pirouette to the left.

instructions.instructions: Set a single parallette, low bar, or dumbbells 1-2 inches from the base of a wall. Face the wall, grab the bar or dumbbells with your normal handstand width, and kick up into a back-to-wall handstand. Let your feet touch the wall and support your handstand. Be sure you have full scapular elevation and pivot your body 180-degrees around to an under-grip belly-to-wall handstand. Your left hand should remain in position on the bar during this pirouette. Allow your feet to come off the wall during rotation, stay tight throughout the pirouette (no arching), and maintain fully elevated shoulders. Pause only briefly in this position and then press through your right hand to pivot back to the start. Switch sides and repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Do not allow the shoulder touching the ear to sag during the pirouette.
2) Do not lift the head when twisting, keep the ears in between the arms.

instructions.instructions: Set a single parallette, low bar, or dumbbells 1-2 inches from the base of a wall. Walk up into a belly-to-wall handstand and once your hands reach the bar or dumbbells, reverse your grip to an under-grip. Your palms should now be facing away from the wall. Be sure you have full scapular elevation and pivot your body 180-degrees around to an overgrip back-to-wall handstand. Your left hand should remain in position on the bar during this pirouette. Allow your feet to come off the wall during rotation, stay tight throughout the pirouette (no arching), and maintain fully elevated shoulders. Pause only briefly in this position and then press through your right hand to pivot back to the start. Switch sides and repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Perform an under-grip pirouette to the right immediately followed over-grip pirouette to the right completes the first half of the repetition.
2) Reversing both movements back to center completes the second half of the repetition.

instructions.instructions: Set a long low bar, or a pair of dumbbells, 1-2 inches from the base of a wall. Face the wall, grab the bar or dumbbells with your normal handstand width, and kick up into a back-to-wall handstand. Let your feet touch the wall and support your handstand. Be sure you have full scapular elevation and pivot your body 180-degrees around to an under-grip belly-to-wall handstand. Now press through your left arm and rotate another 180-degrees in the same direction, returning to a back-to-wall over grip handstand. Allow your feet to come off the wall during rotation, stay tight throughout the pirouette (no arching), and maintain fully elevated shoulders. Reverse the two rotations back to the start and repeat for reps before switching sides to initiate the full pirouette from the opposite arm.

focusPoints.description: 1) Keeping the ribs in and back flat will make it much easier to initiate the pirouette.
2) Regrasp the bar with that shoulder already fully elevated.

instructions.instructions: Set a long low bar, or a pair of dumbbells, 1-2 inches from the base of a wall. Walk up into a belly-to-wall handstand and once your hands reach the bar or dumbbells, reverse your grip to an under grip. Your palms should now be facing away from the wall. Let your feet touch the wall and support your handstand. Be sure you have full scapular elevation and pivot your body 180-degrees around to an overgrip back-to-wall handstand. Now press through your left arm and rotate another 180-degrees in the same direction, back to a belly-to-wall under-grip handstand. Allow your feet to come off the wall during rotation, stay tight throughout the pirouette (no arching), and maintain fully elevated shoulders. Reverse the two rotations back to the start and repeat for reps before switching sides to initiate the full pirouette from the opposite arm.

focusPoints.description: 1) On a single bar the wrists do the majority of the work for rebalancing.
2) Expect the forearms to fatigue quickly during this variation.

instructions.instructions: Kick up into an overgrip free handstand on a single bar. Achieve proper body alignment and full scapular elevation. Your wrists will now have to do the majority of the rebalancing. Due to the small base of support, expect all balance errors to be magnified. Maintain proper shoulder flexion with your sternum pulled in to prevent your back from arching. Hold for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) Failure to maintain proper shoulder flexion with the sternum pulled in will result in the back arching.
2) Due to the small base of support expect all balance errors to be magnified.

instructions.instructions: Kick up into an under-grip free handstand on a single bar. Achieve proper body alignment and full scapular elevation. Your wrists will now have to do the majority of the rebalancing. Due to the small base of support, expect all balance errors to be magnified. Maintain proper shoulder flexion with your sternum pulled in to prevent your back from arching. Hold for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) Push off with the free hand to help initiate the pirouette.
2) Show a controlled single bar handstand before returning back to two bars.

instructions.instructions: Handstand Half Pirouette: Begin in a properly aligned free handstand on parallettes. Be sure you have full scapular elevation, press through your left hand, and pivot your body 90-degrees to the right to achieve an overgrip single-bar handstand. Your right hand should remain in position as your left matches on the same parallette. Stay tight throughout the rotation (no arching), maintain fully elevated shoulders, and pause momentarily in a controlled single-bar handstand. Press through your left hand to pivot back to the start. Repeat for reps and then switch sides.

focusPoints.description: 1) Most right handers normally turn to the left for this drill (counter clockwise); however if you have a strong preference for turning in the other direction, you may do so.
2) Remember to press down strongly on the second support hand as you pirouette in back to center.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a properly aligned free handstand on parallettes. Be sure you have full scapular elevation, press through your left hand, and pivot your body 90-degrees to the right to achieve an overgrip single-bar handstand. Your right hand should remain in position as your left matches on the same parallette. Now quickly press through your right hand and rotate back to the parallette handstand facing the opposite direction. Perform two more 90-degree rotations to complete the full 360-degree pirouette. Show control in each single bar and parallette handstand as you rotate. Most right handers normally turn to the left for this drill (counter-clockwise). However, if you have a strong preference for turning in the other direction, you may do so. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Must touch the shoulder for the rep to count. Almost touching, almost counts.
2) Reach for the floor of the next rep with the scapula already FULLY elevated.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a free handstand and straddle your legs apart wide. Shift some weight to right arm and take your left off the ground. Tap your left shoulder with your left hand, place it back on the floor, and continue to switch sides. Maintain proper alignment and reach for the floor with your scapula fully elevated. You must touch your shoulder for a rep to count; almost touching, almost counts.

focusPoints.description: 1) Generally using a single layer of a 1" panel mat, or something of similar height, is sufficient to obtain an excellent stretch.

instructions.instructions: Achieve a belly-to-wall handstand with your hands a few inches away from the wall and your fingers elevated approximately one inch. A single layer of panel mat or similar padding placed at the base of your first knuckle will sufficiently elevate your fingers. Keep your palms in contact with the floor and hold this handstand elevated wrist stretch for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) Pike the hips slightly so that the feet come just forward of the hips; not 'down', just forward.
2) Drop a leg towards the floor without actively lifting the other leg; simply allow it to rise naturally as the first leg drops.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a free handstand and straddle your legs apart wide. Pike your hips slightly so that your feet come just in front of your hips (not down, just forward). Drop your right leg sideways toward the floor without actively lifting your left. As your right foot lowers down to the side, allow your left leg to rise naturally and your right knee to bend comfortably. Keep your upper body completely fixed and stable and lower your right toes to the floor just outside your right palm. Return to the straddle handstand and continue to switch sides for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Increase the effectiveness of this stretch by keeping the wrist completely square.

instructions.instructions: Begin kneeling on the floor a few inches from a wall and place your palms down flat, fingers facing your knees. Elevate your fingers approximately one inch by placing a single layer of panel mat or similar padding at the base of your first knuckle. Kick up into a properly aligned back-to-wall handstand. Keep your palms in contact with the floor and fingers elevated as you hold this handstand wrist stretch for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) Do NOT allow the back to arch or the shoulders to pike while in the tuck.
2) If either occurs, the scapula are not elevating and protracting strongly enough to maintain proper alignment.

instructions.instructions: From a controlled and properly aligned free handstand, slowly tuck your knees toward your chest until you have a 90-degree bend at your hips. Keep your feet pulled over your glutes. Maintain this position and do not allow your back to arch or shoulders to pike; if either occur, you are not elevating and protracting your scapula strongly enough. Hold for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) Proper body alignment is critical during these; neutral chin, sternum in, ribs down, flat back,protracted and elevated scapula.
2) Make full round circles with the hands that go forward and behind the head.

instructions.instructions: Begin standing facing away from a fixed resistance band set to approximately shoulder height. Grab both handles and step away to create tension in each handle. Raise your arms overhead and achieve proper body alignment. You must have a neutral chin, sternum in, ribs down, flat back, and a protracted and elevated scapula. Make full round circles with your hands that go forward and behind your head. Repeat for reps in both directions before ending each set.

focusPoints.description: 1) The body must show a single straight line from the hands on the floor, through the shoulders and up to the hips. The only bend in the body should be the hinging at the hips.

2) The legs being so far forward of the body's center of mass puts a tremendous strain on the trapezius which in turn will cause the shoulders to collapse and pike; if strong enough protraction is not maintained.

instructions.instructions: From a controlled and properly aligned free handstand, slowly pike your legs down until you have a 90-degree bend at your hips. Keep your legs tight and straight and hold this position. Your body must show a single, straight line from your hands, through your shoulders, and up to your hips. The only bend in your body should be the pike at your hips. Holding your legs so far forward of your body's center of mass puts a tremendous strain on your trapezius muscles. This will cause your shoulders to collapse and pike if strong enough protraction is not maintained. Hold for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) The ribs have a tendency to flare out on these if allowed.
2) Keep the back flat and the sternum pulled in.

instructions.instructions: Begin standing facing a fixed resistance band set to approximately shoulder height. Grab both handles and step away to create tension in each handle. Raise your arms overhead and achieve proper body alignment. You must have a neutral chin, sternum in, ribs down, flat back, and a protracted and elevated scapula. Make full round circles with your hands that go forward and behind your head. Repeat for reps in both directions before ending each set.

focusPoints.description: 1) Grip the blocks with either two (index, middle) or three fingers (index, middle, ring) on the front edge of the block.
2) Shoulder taps must begin and end with a controlled handstand that is held for the designated number of seconds.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a free handstand on handstand blocks. Grip the blocks with either two (index, middle) or three fingers (index, middle, ring) on the front edge of the block. Straddle your legs apart wide, shift some weight to your right arm, and take your left off the block. Tap your left shoulder with your left hand, place it back on the block, and continue to switch sides slowly and with control. Maintain proper alignment and reach for the block with your scapula already fully elevated. You must touch your shoulder for a rep to count; almost touching, almost counts. Shoulder taps must begin and end with a controlled handstand that is held for the designated number of seconds. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Adjust the spacing so that blocks 1 & 3 and blocks 2 & 4 are shoulder width apart.
2) Note that the intent of this drill is NOT to spend time in a static handstand on blocks 2 and 3; but rather to learn to smoothly transfer weight onto and off the supporting shoulder.

instructions.instructions: Place four handstand blocks in a line. Adjust the spacing so that blocks one and three and blocks two and four are shoulder-width apart. Enter a free handstand on blocks one and three, straddle your legs apart wide, and shift your left hand to block two. Shift your right to block four, step back to the start, and continue to walk side-to-side for reps. The intent of this drill is not to spend time in a static handstand on blocks but rather to learn to smoothly transfer weight onto and off of your supporting shoulder.

focusPoints.description: 1) A further refinement of the 2Block Step; the travel will now proceed upward three different levels of height; the block flat, the block turned on its side, the block stood up tall.
2) The stability required on one arm will now increase as it will require slightly longer to manipulate and turn the block to the desired edge.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a free handstand on handstand blocks. Grip the blocks with either two (index, middle) or three fingers (index, middle, ring) on the front edge of the block. Straddle your legs apart wide and shift some weight to your right arm. Slide the left block out to the side and place your hand flat on the floor where it was positioned. Do the same with your right and then reverse the step down by reaching for the left block, sliding it back under your shoulder, and re-gripping it. Do the same with your right, count that as one rep, and repeat.

focusPoints.description: 1) A further refinement of the 2Block Step; the travel will now proceed upward three different levels of height; the block flat, the block turned on its side, the block stood up tall.
2) The stability required on one arm will now increase as it will require slightly longer to manipulate and turn the block to the desired edge.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a free handstand on handstand blocks. Grip the blocks with either two (index, middle) or three fingers (index, middle, ring) on the front edge of the block. Straddle your legs apart wide and shift some weight to your right arm. Flip the left block on its side, shift to your left, and do the same with the right block. Now shift back to your right and stand the left block up tall. Balance on the tall end, do the same with the right block, and reverse the steps back to flat blocks. The stability required on one arm will now increase as it will require slightly longer to manipulate and turn the block to the desired edge. Count that entire sequence as one rep and repeat.

focusPoints.description: 1) When raising from the flat hand up to the fingers, only the elbow should move.
2) Do not allow the free arm to relax or the shoulders to loose their elevation and protraction.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a free handstand with your legs straddled wide. Shift weight over to your right side and come up onto all five of your left fingertips. As your raise up to your fingers, only your elbow should move. Never allow your free arm to relax or your shoulders to lose tension, protraction, or elevation. Keep your supporting shoulder over your supporting hand at all times. Hold for time before switching sides.

Mobility.name: Assisted One Arm Tuck Flag Pulses

focusPoints.description: 1) Note that the assisting arm on the bar is in an under-grip. This grip helps to remind that this arm is assisting balance only; not actively pulling the body up and down.
2) Do not attempt to lean the whole body sideways, instead focus on bending at the waist.

instructions.instructions: To set up, kneel next to stall bars turned 90-degrees to the side so your left side is facing the bars and your right side is facing away. Place your right hand flat about a foot from the bars and under grip a rung at about shoulder height with your left. Enter a handstand with these grips and then tuck your knees and bend sideways at your waist, stretching your left oblique. The under grip is to remind you that that arm is for assisting balance only and not actively pulling your body up and down. Perform swift bounces up and down through this tucked flag position, then hold your lowest leg position for time, and switch sides.

focusPoints.description: 1) The diagonal of the legs comes from allowing the working leg to drop naturally from the hip; do not overly arch the obliques.
2) Beware the hips twisting when pushing up into the finger assisted OAHS. Keeping the hips slightly piked and back flat will help to prevent this.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a free handstand with your legs straddled wide. Shift weight over to your right side and come up onto your left three fingers (index, middle, and thumb). As your raise up to your fingers, only your elbow should move. Never allow your free arm to relax or your shoulders to lose tension, protraction, or elevation. Keep your supporting shoulder over your supporting hand at all times. Hold for time before switching sides.

Mobility.name: assisted one arm tuck flag pulls

focusPoints.description: 1) Keep the hips square; do not allow one to drift forward or backward of the other. Set up a phone or camera from the side to ensure there is no twisting.
2) Staying square will make a tremendous difference in how stable and in control this integrated mobility element feels.

instructions.instructions: To set up, kneel next to stall bars turned 90-degrees to the side so your left side is facing the bars and your right side is facing away. Place your right hand flat about a foot from the bars and under-grip a rung at about shoulder height with your left. Enter a handstand with these grips then tuck your knees, and bend sideways at your waist, stretching your left oblique. Go as low as you can while keeping proper upper body alignment. Pause and pull back up until your knees stack back over your hips. The under-grip is to remind you that that arm is for assisting balance only and not actively pulling your body up and down. Keep your knees tucked and repeat for reps, achieving your lowest leg position each time. Switch sides and repeat.

focusPoints.description: 1) Push down firmly into the ground causing the scapula to elevate and the shoulder to touch the ear.
2) At the same time keep the supporting shoulder directly above the supporting hand.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a free handstand with your legs straddled wide. Shift weight over to your right side and come up onto your left index finger. As your raise up to your fingers, only your elbow should move. Never allow your free arm to relax or your shoulders to lose tension, protraction, or elevation. Keep your supporting shoulder over your supporting hand at all times. Hold for time before switching sides.

focusPoints.description: 1) Note how the far leg drops directly over and out to the side while the other leg pulls down and around to the front.
2) Although the obliques are arching strongly, the supporting shoulder continues to remain directly above the supporting hand.

instructions.instructions: To set up, kneel next to stall bars turned 90-degrees to the side so your left side is facing the bars and your right side is facing away. Place your right hand flat about a foot from the bars and under grip a rung at about shoulder height with your left. Enter a handstand with these grips and then straddle your legs wide. Scissor your legs and simultaneously arch strongly to your right side. Go as low as possible without your supporting shoulder moving out of alignment. Pull back to the straddle and repeat for reps before switching sides.

focusPoints.description: 1) Don't think hips over arm; rather think working leg DOWN which automatically will raise the opposite leg and then push through the shoulder (remember shoulder touching the ear!) which will center the hips over the supporting arm.
2) Correct imbalances with the wrists and by piking/opening the hips; do not attempt to planche the shoulder to save balance as is done in a two arm handstand.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a free handstand with your legs straddled wide. Shift some weight to your right arm and take your left hand off the ground. As you shift onto your right arm, don't think hips over arm; think working side's leg down. This will automatically will raise your opposite leg. Now push through your right shoulder (remember, your shoulder must be touching your ear). This will center your hips over your supporting arm. Correct imbalances with your wrists and by piking your hips. Do not attempt to planche your shoulder to save balance as is done in a two-arm handstand. Hold for time and switch sides.

focusPoints.description: 1) When rolling from the back to the stomach do not allow the chest to touch the ground
2) When rolling from the stomach to the back do not allow the shoulder blades to touch the ground

instructions.instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and arms overhead. Press your lower back firmly into the floor and lift your legs just off the ground. Simultaneously bring your shoulder blades just off the floor and as you do so, do not allow your lower back to lose contact with the floor. Keep your biceps by your ears and body fully extended as you roll over your right side and onto your stomach into an arch body hold. During the sideways roll, lift your thighs, chest, and arms as high as possible. Pause here only briefly and roll right again, back to the hollow body. When you roll to the arch, never let your chest touch the floor; when you roll to your back, never let your shoulder blades touch. Roll as smoothly as you can and repeat for an even number of reps in each direction.

focusPoints.description: 1) Do not allow the lower back to arch; maintain proper protracting and PPT (posterior pelvic tilt) at all times during the rep
2) In the beginning you may decrease the intensity by rolling up onto either the knees, the forearms or both

instructions.instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and arms overhead. Press your lower back firmly into the floor and lift your legs just off the floor. Simultaneously bring your shoulder blades just off the ground and, as you do so, do not allow your lower back to lose contact with the floor. Keep your biceps by your ears and body fully extended as you roll to your right side, into a long hollow hold. As soon as your right hand and foot make contact with the floor, begin pressing through them. Maintain posterior pelvic tilt (PPT) throughout the sideways roll, pause momentarily in the long hollow, and roll right again to return to the hollow body position. Constant leg, glute, and ab tension is critical for preventing low back arch. You can decrease the intensity by rolling onto either your knees, forearms, or both. Roll as smoothly as you can and repeat for an even number of reps in each direction.

focusPoints.description: 1) Use the height of the high candle up onto the shoulders to provide power into the downward roll
2) Turn the bottom shin 90 degrees sideways to smoothly roll up to the modified lunge

instructions.instructions: Half Shoulder Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) Making a large circle with the right arm on top will make initiating the roll much easier
2) Note that the back of the right shoulder is the first to touch the ground; not the neck or head

instructions.instructions: Kneeling Shoulder Roll (Right Side)

focusPoints.description: 1) Roll diagonally across the back from the left shoulder blade down to the right hip
2) At this stage in training, 'smooth' is more important than fast

instructions.instructions: Kneeling Shoulder Roll (Left Side)

focusPoints.description: 1) Make sure to step forward with the same foot as the shoulder you are going to roll with
2) For example for a right shoulder roll steps forward with the right foot

instructions.instructions: Shoulder Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) Maintaining PPT allow the body to smoothly fall backward in the roll
2) Keep the back curled with the sternum pulled in and chin tucked toward the chest

instructions.instructions: Rock and Roll to Squat

focusPoints.description: 1) Begin with hands on floor, feet on mat and hips up higher than the shoulders
2) Do NOT land on the head or the neck; rather land on the back of the shoulders

instructions.instructions: Assisted Forward Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) Reach for the ground with bent elbows
2) Look at the belly button to correctly position the head and neck for the roll

instructions.instructions: Forward Tuck Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) The knees will momentarily extend and straighten in the middle of the roll
2) Keep the chin tucked firmly down on the chest

instructions.instructions: Extended Forward Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) To initiate pull the hips up over the head and the head under the hips simultaneously
2) Before the feet touch the ground place the hands on the floor in between the legs; not outside

instructions.instructions: Forward Straddle Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) Keep the chest folded as tightly to the legs as possible during this roll
2) Use of a soft surface is necessary here as the body rolls up onto the heels first

instructions.instructions: Forward Pike Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) At the peak of the rock backward, place the hands flat on the floor next to your ears
2) If you are unable to place the hands on the floor, your hips did not roll up high enough during the rock backward

instructions.instructions: Pressure Rock and Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) Keep the glutes close to the feet when squatting down
2) Continue rolling backward until those hands are FLAT on the floor next to the ears

instructions.instructions: Pressure Rock and Roll to Stand

focusPoints.description: 1) Before beginning, first adjust position on the panel mat so that when laying down the shoulders are firmly on the mat, but the neck and head extend out past the edge of the mat
2) Continue working on the panel, gradually reducing the height one layer at a time until you are finally working on a single layer of panel mat

instructions.instructions: Assisted Backward Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) Feel the weight of the backward roll on the arms; not the neck
2) If pressure is felt in the neck, the hands did not get to the floor and begin pushing down soon enough

instructions.instructions: Backward Tuck Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) Reach between the legs toward the ground; not outside the legs
2) Bend the elbows to soften the landing upon the ground

instructions.instructions: Backward Straddle Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) Lean the torso strongly forward as the hips press backwards during the descent
2) Stay leaning forward as the glutes fall upon the ground and the body begins to roll over

instructions.instructions: Backward Pike Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) Press up ever so slightly out of the headstand to initiate the roll
2) If you are not strong enough to press up slightly, you are not yet strong enough to begin headstand forward rolls

instructions.instructions: Headstand Forward Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) Use a controlled descent into the roll
2) The back of the head may lightly brush the mat, however only the back of the shoulders should bear the full load of bodyweight during the roll

instructions.instructions: Assisted Bent Arm Handstand Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) Begin in a very high semi-planche position with the body straight, but the shoulders piked and directly above the hands
2) Initiate the roll by leaning the shoulders far in front of the hands

instructions.instructions: High Planche Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) Keep the arms absolutely straight and locked during the roll
2) As the feet slide down keep them in contact with the wall as long as possible

instructions.instructions: Sliding Planche Roll

Handstand Forward Roll.name: Assisted Lock Arm Handstand Forward Roll

Strength.name: Assisted Lock Arm Handstand Forward Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) Do not allow the feet to fall forward when the shoulders begin their forward lean
2) If landing flat on the back rather than rolling smoothly, the feet failed to stay stacked vertically as long as possible

instructions.instructions: Assisted Straight Arm Handstand Forward Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) Note in the video how the feet, hips and shoulders remain in a vertical stack almost until the back of the shoulders touch the ground
2) The only change in body position during the roll is the piking of the shoulders forward in front of the hands

instructions.instructions: Straight Arm Handstand Forward Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) Begin extending the body when the knees reach vertical during the roll backward
2) Keep the chin tucked

instructions.instructions: Backward Roll to Front Support

focusPoints.description: 1) Push upward and backward to land in the long hollow position
2) No sagging; already be in strong protraction and posterior pelvic tilt prior to the feet touching the ground

instructions.instructions: Backward Roll to Long Hollow

focusPoints.description: 1) Setting proper distance from the wall is very important. To do so lay on the floor with the head approximately twelve to eighteen inches from the wall. Now without fidgeting, sit up on the floor, pull the feet into the glutes and then stand. This is the starting position.
2) If the feet are contacting the wall with the arms still bent; the press with the arms was too slow. If the body is far past vertical when the feet touch the wall, the legs were too slow extending

instructions.instructions: Assisted Bent Arm Back Extension

Back Extension Development.name: Assisted Lock Arm Backward Roll to Long Hollow

Strength.name: Assisted Lock Arm Backward Roll to Long Hollow

focusPoints.description: 1) Use straight locked internally rotated arms with the fingers pointing towards each other
2) Strongly protract; think of pulling the sternum in and down

instructions.instructions: Assisted Straight Arm Backward Roll to Long Hollow

Back Extension Development.name: Lock Arm Back Extension to Long Hollow

Strength.name: Lock Arm Back Extension to Long Hollow

focusPoints.description: 1) Reaching back behind the head, begin pressing downward strongly with straight arms as soon as the hands contact the floor
2) A great deal of trapezius strength is required to maintain the arms in this position under full bodyweight load

instructions.instructions: Straight Arm Back Extension to Long Hollow

focusPoints.description: 1) When rolling backward look upward towards the ceiling
2) If you are in the correct position you should be able to see your toes

instructions.instructions: Straight Arm Back Extension

focusPoints.description: 1) Reach the hands far outside the feet to begin. Finish with the feet far outside the hands as well
2) Press down strongly and use the traps to lift the hips; do not simply jump with the legs

instructions.instructions: Cartwheel Press

focusPoints.description: 1) Note how the cartwheel begins with the same lunge as a lunge kick to handstand
2) As the hands reach toward the floor with a quarter turn of the torso kick the rear leg up strongly

instructions.instructions: Cartwheel (Right Side)

focusPoints.description: 1) Performing cartwheels on a straight floor line is very helpful for smoothing out performance and alignment errors

2) For a left cartwheel the four points of contact should land on the line in the following order; left hand, right hand, right foot, left foot. For a right cartwheel; right hand, left hand, left foot, right foot

instructions.instructions: Cartwheel (Left Side)

focusPoints.description: 1) Reach forward with the right arm and keep the left arm up near the left ear
2) Do not allow the hips to pike during the cartwheel

instructions.instructions: Cartwheel Series (Right Side)

focusPoints.description: 1) Do not look where the body is traveling; rather keep the gaze focused directly in front of you
2) It is easier to stand if the left foot is pulled in closer to the left hand when setting that foot down

instructions.instructions: Cartwheel Series (Left Side)

focusPoints.description: 1) When turning between cartwheels pivot so that the stomach is turning forward rather than the back
2) Remember to bend the front knee when lunging into the next cartwheel

instructions.instructions: Alternating Cartwheel

focusPoints.description: 1) Use your favorite side cartwheel for these. Remember to stay upright; no hunching forward
2) Bending each of the knees when landing greatly increases the speed with which you can get into the next repetition

instructions.instructions: Speed Cartwheel

focusPoints.description: 1) Using your favorite side cartwheel; place the working arm up by your ear and the non-working arm tucked behind your back
2) Arch the obliques to get the first foot on the floor quickly

instructions.instructions: Near Hand Cartwheel

focusPoints.description: 1) With the working arm up by the ear, think of reaching up and over the head to place the hand on the ground
2) Do not allow the working arm to reach across the face; this will result in very poor support strength during the cartwheel

instructions.instructions: Far Hand Cartwheel

Integrated Roll Series.name: Stretch Forward Roll to Pike Jump Handstand with a Half Pirouette

Strength.name: Stretch Forward Roll to Pike Jump Handstand with a Half Pirouette

focusPoints.description: 1) Remember that this is a jump to handstand, not a press to handstand, so use those legs!
2) Keep the pirouetting arm pressed firmly next to the ear

instructions.instructions: Stretch Forward Roll to Pike Jump Handstand with a Half Pirouette

Integrated Roll Series.name: Lock Arm Handstand Forward Roll to Pike Jump Handstand with a Full Pirouette

Strength.name: Lock Arm Handstand Forward Roll to Pike Jump Handstand with a Full Pirouette

focusPoints.description: 1) Note that there are four hand placements or steps during the full pirouette
2) Note also how close the hands come together during the second step of the full pirouette

instructions.instructions: Straight Arm Handstand Forward Roll to Pike Jump Handstand with a Full Pirouette

focusPoints.description: 1) Maintain form and complete extension at all times
2) Do not lift the chin during the pirouette, keep it relatively low and look at your thumbs thru your eyebrow using your peripheral vision

instructions.instructions: Handstand Forward Roll Series

Integrated Roll Series.name: Back Extension Half Pirouette to Lock Arm Handstand Forward Pike Roll

Strength.name: Back Extension Half Pirouette to Lock Arm Handstand Forward Pike Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) To initiate the twist it helps to reach the supporting arm slightly past the midline of the body when pressing the straight arms back behind you in the beginning of the roll

2) If you are twisting to the right the fingers of your right hand will be turned inward upon contact with the floor behind your head. If twisting to the left the fingers of the left hand will be turned inward

instructions.instructions: Back Extension Half Pirouette to Lock Arm Handstand Forward Pike Roll

focusPoints.description: 1) Interesting there are only three steps taken during a back extension full pirouette
2) If you lift the head early during the twist, you will fall out short of the handstand

instructions.instructions: Back Extension Full Pirouette

focusPoints.description: 1) Finish all final positions of each element in the series cleanly; for example show a straight handstand after completing the Handstand Forward Roll Half Pirouette
2) The goal here is for the entire series to flow smoothly with no obvious technical errors or rhythm breaks

instructions.instructions: Back Extension Series

focusPoints.description: 1) A false grip should have a 90 degree bend in the wrist.
2) The hands should pull together in the center of the chest.

instructions.instructions: Begin standing between a pair of gymnastic rings set to head height and false grip them. You should now have the bottom of your palms (not your wrists), in contact with the lower, center portion of the rings and a 90-degree bend in your wrists. Maintain your false grips and pull into a lock-off. Pull your hands together, palms facing in, and keep them touching your chest as you hold the false grip lock-off for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) Initially straight arms make the FG quite difficult to hold.
2) If you lose the false grip, stop & do not count that set.

instructions.instructions: Begin standing between a pair of gymnastic rings set to head height and false grip them. You should now have the bottom of your palms, and not your wrists in contact with the lower, center portion of the rings and a 90-degree bend in your wrists. Maintain your false grips and weight the rings until you are in a dead hang and hold for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) If your false grip keeps slipping out, your forearms may need time to gradually increase their strength and flexibility.

instructions.instructions: Set the rings to a height that allows your back to be just off the ground with your arms fully extended. Your arms and the ring straps should be in one straight line, perpendicular to the floor. False grip the rings and get your body as close to parallel with the floor as your situation allows. Ensure that your feet are your only contact with the ground and row straight up until your shoulders touch your hands. Descend with control and maintain 90-degrees wrist angles. Maintain an even tempo, a straight body line, and proper posterior pelvic tilt (PPT) as you repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) While in a FG, pull up until the hands touch the chest.
2) The elbows must completely straighten between reps.

instructions.instructions: Begin from a dead hand on gymnastic rings with a proper false grip. Perform a pull-up, touching your hands to your chest while maintaining the false grip. Lower down back to a straight arm hang and check that you still have a 90-degree wrist bend. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Do not overly assist with the legs; just barely use them.
2) It is not necessary to straighten the arms at the top.

instructions.instructions: Set a pair of gymnastic rings to just below chest height. Stand between them, grab ahold of them in a false grip, and, staying on your feet, lower down below them until your arms straighten. Row back up until your chest touches the rings. Now get your chest above the rings into the bottom of a dip by keeping the rings close to your body and shifting your shoulders forward. This should move your elbows back behind your torso. You must maintain the false grip throughout the pull and transition. Now that your chest is above the rings, pause momentarily. Now reverse the transition, row back down, and repeat for reps. Keep your feet on the ground throughout but use your legs as little as possible.

focusPoints.description: 1) Descend with control; do not simply flop down.
2) Do not allow the elbows to prematurely drop backward.

instructions.instructions: Set a pair of gymnastic rings so that your feet can reach the floor or a box when in the bottom of a dip. Begin in a top support above the rings with your arms completely straight and rings turned out past parallel (rotate the rings to the outside). Perform a controlled eccentric dip, make contact with the floor, and use your feet to assist lowering through the transition and false grip pull-up. Lower yourself completely below the rings while maintaining a false grip. Use your feet to assist as you pull back up, transition, and dip out. The entire ascent can be a dynamic movement. Achieve a proper and stable top support and repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Move as slowly as possible through the transition.
2) Note how the elbows circle from up, to back, to down.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a top support above the rings with your arms completely straight and rings turned out past parallel (rotate the rings to the outside). Perform a controlled eccentric dip, transition down to the top of a false grip pull-up, and lower yourself completely below the rings with control while maintaining a false grip. Use your feet to step back up to a proper and stable top support and repeat this eccentric muscle-up for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) This position should feel as though you are pressing the crease of your elbows strongly forward into the straps.

instructions.instructions: Strap Ring Plank: Set a pair of gymnastic rings just off the floor. Be sure you have a set of leverage assisted ring strength straps (LARS straps) attached. Slip your arms through the straps, fix them around the thickest part of your forearm, and grab ahold of the rings. Assume a proper straight arm plank position with your shoulders over your hands. Turn the rings outward, past parallel, and hold for time. This position should feel as though you are pressing the crease of your elbows strongly forward into the straps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Keep the rings turned out past parallel at all times during both directions of plank circles.

instructions.instructions: Set a pair of gymnastic rings just off the floor. Be sure you have a set of leverage assisted ring strength straps (LARS straps) attached. Slip your arms through the straps, fix them around the thickest part of your forearm, and grab ahold of the rings. Assume a proper straight arm plank position with your shoulders over your hands. Turn the rings outward, past parallel, and keep them this way throughout the exercise. First, perform a set of outward circles with the rings, then switch directions and perform the same number of inward circles.

focusPoints.description: 1) Lower until your chest is level with your shoulders.
2) Only go as low as you can keep your elbows straight.

instructions.instructions: Set a pair of gymnastic rings just off the floor. Be sure you have a set of leverage assisted ring strength straps (LARS straps) attached. Slip your arms through the straps, fix them around the thickest part of your forearm, and grab ahold of the rings. Assume a proper straight arm plank position with your shoulders over your hands. Turn the rings outward, past parallel, and then push your hands straight out to the side. Be sure you maintain straight elbows and a 90-degree armpit angle as you lower. Descend until your chest is level with your shoulders (your arms should make a letter T shape) and press back up to plank. As no time should your elbows bend. Use the straps to help you keep your arms straight and repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) At a minimum, the rings must be turned past parallel.
2) Lean strongly on the straps as you press the elbows fwd.

instructions.instructions: Set a pair of gymnastic rings to at least shoulder height. Be sure you have a set of leverage assisted ring strength straps (LARS straps) attached. Slip your arms through the straps, fix them around the thickest part of your forearm, and grab ahold of the rings. Hop up to a top support above the rings. Straighten your elbows and turn the rings out past parallel. Achieve a completely vertical body line. Strongly press your elbows forward, lean on the straps, and hold for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) Keep tension on the strap by pressing the elbows forward.
2) There should be daylight between the torso and the arms.

instructions.instructions: Set a pair of gymnastic rings to at least shoulder height. Be sure you have a set of leverage assisted ring strength straps (LARS straps) attached. Slip your arms through the straps, fix them around the thickest part of your forearm, and grab ahold of the rings. Hop up to a top support above the rings. Straighten your elbows and turn the rings out past parallel. Achieve a completely vertical body line. Strongly press your elbows forward, lean on the straps, and then begin to swing your body forward and backward. As you swing, keep your body as tight as possible and press your elbows forward to maintain pressure on the straps. There should be daylight between your torso and arms between every forward and backward ring swing. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) A 45 degree angle is sufficient turnout for this exercise.
2) The elbows will now be pressing forward unassisted.

instructions.instructions: Set two parallettes on boxes at least waist-high and turn them outward 45-degrees. Stand between the boxes, grab the parallettes, and hop up to a top support over them. Your hands should be turned out. Straighten your elbows and press them forward, depress your shoulder blades, and keep your body tight. Hold for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) Ring planks are extremely biceps intensive.
2) The elbows should be pressed completely straight.

instructions.instructions: Set a pair of gymnastic rings just off the floor. Grab ahold of the rings and assume a proper straight arm plank position with your shoulders over your hands. Turn the rings outward, past parallel, and hold for time. In this position, you should feel as though you are pressing the crease of your elbows strongly forward.

focusPoints.description: 1) Press the arms outward until they are clear of your hips.
2) Bend your wrists if necessary to keep forearms off straps.

instructions.instructions: Set a pair of gymnastic rings to at least shoulder height. Grab ahold of the rings and hop up to a top support above the rings. Straighten your elbows, strongly depress your shoulder blades, and turn the rings out past parallel. Achieve a completely vertical body line. Press your arms out slightly to keep your hands clear of your hips. Bend your wrists if necessary to keep your forearms off of the top of the ring straps. Strongly press forward through your elbows and hold for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) The intent is to perform the 1/2 L-sit without changing your basic arm and torso position.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a proper top support above gymnastic rings. Without changing your torso and arm position, lift your knees up so they are together and level with your hips. Extend your feet out until they are hanging just below your knees and hold this half L-sit position for time. Keep strong scapular depression, straight elbows, and the rings turned out past parallel throughout.

focusPoints.description: 1) The chest is tall with only a slight degree of protraction.
2) Do not bend the elbows or pull the arms into the sides.

instructions.instructions: Begin in a proper top support above gymnastic rings. Without changing your torso and arm position, lift your straight legs up until they are parallel with the floor (level with your hips). Keep strong scapular depression, straight elbows, and the rings turned out past parallel throughout. Do not let your chest cave in as you hold this rings L-sit for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) Elevate the knees until they are above the hips.
2) Do not allow your legs to lay on or touch the arms.

instructions.instructions: Hop up above gymnastic rings as you would to enter a top support. As you ascend, straddle your legs apart, bring them level with your hips, and bend your knees. When your elbows straighten, the rings should be between your thighs. Turn the rings out past parallel, depress your shoulders, and lift your knees above your hips. Keep your feet under your knees. Do not allow your thighs to touch your arms, and hold this ring half straddle L for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) To properly balance, the chest will need to lean forward.
2) DO NOT allow the legs to rest on the arms or rings.

instructions.instructions: Hop up above gymnastic rings as you would to enter a top support. As you ascend, straddle your legs apart wide, bring them to hip height, and lock your knees. When your elbows straighten, the rings should be between your thighs. Turn the rings out past parallel, depress your shoulders, and lift your feet above your hips. To balance, you must lean your chest forward. Do not allow your thighs to touch your arms as you hold the ring straddle L for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) Despite moving, the arms should remain locked in place.
2) Swinging forward and backward is one repetition.

instructions.instructions: Set a pair of gymnastic rings to approximately shoulder height. Grab them, take a few steps backward, and take a few swift forward steps as you hop up into top support. Hold your body straight and still as the rings swing you back and forth. Keep the rings fixed just outside of your hips as you swing for the set.

focusPoints.description: 1) The hips need to swing in front of and behind the hands.
2) Daylight should be visible in between the hips and hands.

instructions.instructions: Set a pair of gymnastic rings to at least shoulder height. Grab ahold of the rings and hop up to a proper top support above the rings. Straighten your elbows and turn the rings out past parallel. Achieve a completely vertical body line, strongly press your elbows forward, and then begin to swing your body forward and backward. As you swing, keep your body as tight as possible and press your elbows forward to maintain stability. There should be daylight between your torso and arms between every forward and backward ring swing. Repeat for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Use the feet on the ground to control the intensity.
2) Allow the knees to bend, but keep the hips open and flat.

instructions.instructions: Set a pair of gymnastic rings to approximately head height. Grab ahold of them, pull up slightly, and tuck your knees toward your chest. Keep a solid grip on the rings and spin backward 360-degrees. Lower your legs back to the floor and straighten your elbows. Turn the rings so your palms are facing backward, fully extend your hips, and retract your shoulder blades. Use your feet and knee bend to adjust the intensity of this position as you hold for time. Keep your chest open, hips extended, and elbows locked throughout the assisted German hang.

focusPoints.description: 1) Descend completely into complete shoulder extension.
2) Turn the palms outward so that they point straight back.

instructions.instructions: Set a pair of gymnastic rings well overhead. Grab ahold of them, pull up slightly, and tuck your knees toward your chest. Keep a solid grip on the rings and spin backward 360-degrees. Extend your legs, straighten your elbows, and hang freely from full shoulder extension. Turn the rings so your palms are facing backward, fully extend your hips, and retract your shoulder blades. Keep your chest open, hips extended, and elbows locked throughout the German hang.

focusPoints.description: 1) Descend completely at the bottom of each repetition.
2) Smoothly pull up out of the bottom; no jerking.

instructions.instructions: Set a pair of gymnastic rings well overhead. Grab ahold of them, pull up slightly, and tuck your knees toward your chest. Keep a solid grip on the rings and spin backward 360-degrees. Extend your legs, straighten your elbows, and hang freely from full shoulder extension. Turn the rings so your palms are facing backward, fully extend your hips, and retract your shoulder blades. Keep your chest open, hips extended, and elbows locked. Now, keep straight elbows and knees, and pull your hips back over your shoulders to return to the starting position. Pull in and out of the German hang for reps.

focusPoints.description: 1) Turn the hands outward BEFORE you begin your descent.
2) The hands must remain turned with palm facing back.

instructions.instructions: Begin from an inverted hang on gymnastic rings and tuck your knees toward your chest. Keep a solid grip on the rings and turn them so your palms are facing behind you. Keep the tuck and lower backward with straight elbows until your hips reach shoulder height. Your back should now be parallel to the floor. Avoid squeezing your sides with your arms during the hold. To produce lift and stability, protract slightly and press down through the rings. Keep your hands facing backward and hold this tuck back lever for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) Slightly straddle and slightly pull the knees backward until they are just behind the hips.

instructions.instructions: Begin from an inverted hang on gymnastic rings and tuck your knees toward your chest. Keep a solid grip on the rings and turn them so your palms are facing behind you. Lower backward with straight elbows and as you lower, straddle your legs apart slightly (keep your knees bent 90-degrees). Pull your knees up and slightly back until they are level with your hips. Then lower until they reach shoulder height. Your back should now be flat and parallel to the floor. Avoid squeezing your sides with your arms during the hold; to produce lift and stability, protract slightly and press down through the rings. Keep your hands facing backward and hold this open tuck back lever for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) The knees should be pulled apart with the hips open and flat; similar to the bent arm planche your learned in F2.

instructions.instructions: Begin from an inverted hang on gymnastic rings and bend your knees to 90-degrees. Keep a solid grip on the rings and turn them so your palms are facing behind you. Lower backward with straight elbows and as you lower, straddle your legs apart wide (keep your knees bent 90-degrees). Keep the wide straddle, fully open your hips (no piking) and lower until your hips and legs are horizontal and in line with your shoulders. Your back and straddled thighs should now be flat and parallel to the floor. Avoid squeezing your sides with your arms during the hold. To produce lift and stability, protract slightly and press down through the rings. Keep your hands facing backward, glutes tight, and hold this half straddle back lever for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) Press downward on the rings to produce lift and stability.
2) Do not cheat by pressing the arms into the sides.

instructions.instructions: Begin from an inverted hang on gymnastic rings and extend your hips until you can squeeze your glutes. Bend your knees to 90-degrees, keep a solid grip on the rings, and turn them so your palms are facing behind you. Lower backward with straight elbows and lower until your hips and legs are horizontal, in line with your shoulders. Your back and thighs should now be flat and parallel to the floor. Avoid squeezing your sides with your arms during the hold. To produce lift and stability, protract slightly and press down through the rings. Keep your hands facing backward, glutes, tight, and hold this half back lever for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) Note that rings are still turned outward putting pressure directly on the brachialis.

instructions.instructions: Begin from an inverted hang on gymnastic rings and extend your hips until your body straightens and you can squeeze your glutes. Keep a solid grip on the rings and turn them so your palms are facing behind you. Lower backward with straight elbows until your body is horizontal and in line with your shoulders. As you lower, straddle your legs as wide as you can. Your back and legs should now be flat and parallel to the floor. Avoid squeezing your sides with your arms during the hold. To produce lift and stability, protract slightly and press down through the rings. Keep your hands facing backward, glutes tight, and hold this straddle back lever for time.

focusPoints.description: 1) The body should be completely straight and flat.
2) No sagging, arching or piking; squeeze glutes and abs.

instructions.instructions: Begin from an inverted hang on gymnastic rings and extend your hips until your body straightens and you can squeeze your glutes. Keep a solid grip on the rings and turn them so your palms are facing behind you. Lower backward with straight elbows and a straight body. Lower until your body is horizontal, in line with your shoulders. Your body should now be flat and parallel to the floor. Avoid squeezing your sides with your arms during the hold. To produce lift and stability, protract slightly and press down through the rings. Keep your hands facing backward, glutes tight, and hold this back lever for time.
